nodes.label: tailwind.config.ts
nodes.community_name: Web Tailwind Config and Tokens Preset

nodes.label: A-30 Single tenant (AM-14)
nodes.rationale: Single tenant (AMPM only); no organisation_id column anywhere. AMPM confirmed: for AMPM's internal use, not for licensing. If AMPM intends to license the software, add organisation_id to every root table before build; it is expensive to retrofit.

nodes.label: A-26 Function status versus readiness (AM-3)
nodes.rationale: functions.status (planned, confirmed, cancelled) and functions.readiness_status are two fields; readiness is derived from the function's checklist. AMPM confirmed the readiness rule; the two fields stand. Could merge into one field if AMPM prefers.

nodes.label: A-27 Room category capacity (AM-5)
nodes.rationale: hotel_room_categories.room_count is the inventory in that category; max_occupancy is per room. Not addressed by AMPM; stands.

nodes.label: A-28 Demo data isolation (AM-8)
nodes.rationale: Default: demo data lives in the same database, isolated by client_accounts.is_demo, wedding_projects.is_demo and hotels.demo_visible; demo accounts see a curated subset of real hotels with rate items masked and one sample project. AMPM changed: demo shows up to three locations and one or two sample hotels each with indicative prices and street view, after OTP; limits and duration configurable and to be finalised. A separate demo database would remove the flags and add a copy job.

nodes.label: A-29 Subscription scope (AM-9)
nodes.rationale: A subscription belongs to an account and covers every project on that account. Not addressed by AMPM; stands. Per-wedding subscriptions would add subscriptions.project_id.

nodes.label: A-1 Platform form factor (Q1)
nodes.rationale: Default: responsive web application with one backend for team workspace, client portal and guest portal; no native apps in v1; Phase 4 adds installable PWA mode with read-only offline caching of run-of-show and checklists. AMPM 2026-10-25 changed: native iOS and Android apps with offline use from launch; the web remains for the public website; whether the client portal also needs a web version is open. Schema impact: native apps change nothing except adding a device_tokens table for push notifications; the offline change queue is a client-side store mirrored by audit_events on sync.

nodes.label: A-10 Phase 1 scope (Q10)
nodes.rationale: Default: Phase 1 includes demo/trial, the full ten-status hotel enquiry flow, online payment and a minimal built-in CMS; phase tags per table in §19. AMPM changed: first release includes discovery, wedding management, vendors, client portal, department access, RSVP, requests, live chat and offline operations; excludes website editing, online milestone payments and GST invoicing; single or staged launch to be agreed.

nodes.label: A-11 Notification channels (Q11)
nodes.rationale: Default: in-app, email and WhatsApp (via a business service provider) with SMS fallback, enumerated in notifications.channel. AMPM partly decided: email and WhatsApp required, SMS proposed, providers to be confirmed; live chat added. Unused channels are disabled in configuration.

nodes.label: A-12 Built-in CMS (Q12)
nodes.rationale: Default: minimal built-in CMS (cms_pages, cms_showcase_items) for destinations, showcase items and page copy. AMPM dropped it: no website editing in the app; the website is maintained outside the platform. A headless CMS would replace the two tables with an integration.

nodes.label: A-13 Authentication (Q13)
nodes.rationale: Default: clients sign in with email and password, phone OTP optional second factor; staff must use email, password and an authenticator app (TOTP); guests use token links only and never have accounts. AMPM changed: prospects, demo users and clients sign in with mobile number and OTP; staff method to be finalised (authenticator recommended). Phone-OTP-only makes users.password_hash nullable and adds an OTP flow on auth_tokens.

nodes.label: A-14 Hosting (Q14)
nodes.rationale: Default: hosted in an Indian region with private object storage; no schema impact, noted so retention and residency rules are consistent. AMPM still open: hosting to be confirmed with the developer.

nodes.label: A-15 Sizing (Q15)
nodes.rationale: Default sizing for index and partition choices: up to 50 staff users, 40 concurrent projects, 1,500 guests per project, 500 hotels, 2 TB of media in year one. AMPM changed: about 200 hotels and 20 concurrent weddings; staff and guest capacity to be confirmed. Larger volumes change indexing and partitioning (audit_events, notifications, guest_function_attendance), not the model.

nodes.label: A-16 Currency, GST, language, time zone (Q16)
nodes.norm_label: a-16 currency, gst, language, time zone (q16)
nodes.rationale: Default: single currency INR with a currency column wherever money appears; GST fields on invoices and invoice lines; English only; time zone per project, default Asia/Kolkata. AMPM confirmed INR and English; the platform does not issue GST invoices, so GST fields are dormant. Multi-currency would add exchange-rate snapshots on payments and budget_lines.

nodes.label: A-17 Retention (Q17)
nodes.rationale: Default retention classes: closed leads 24 months; guest personal data 12 months after project close; identity documents checkout plus 30 days; demo data reset on a schedule; retention_class and retention_until on documents and identity_documents, client_access_until on wedding_projects. AMPM changed: no automatic deletion; retention and deletion require AMPM approval; periods to be confirmed; jobs become proposed deletion lists awaiting approval.

nodes.label: A-18 Several hotels and venues per wedding (Q18)
nodes.community_name: Wedding Projects, Rooms and Travel Tables
nodes.norm_label: a-18 several hotels and venues per wedding (q18)
nodes.rationale: Default: a wedding may use several hotels (project_hotels) and venues outside the database (external_venues); wedding_projects.primary_hotel_id is a convenience pointer only. AMPM confirmed multiple hotels and venues per wedding.

nodes.label: A-19 Room blocks and allocations (Q19)
nodes.community_name: Wedding Projects, Rooms and Travel Tables
nodes.rationale: Default: room blocks held per project, hotel, room category and date range; allocations reference a block; occupants are individual guests, children included; sharing rules not enforced by the schema. AMPM confirmed: room blocks by hotel, category and dates; team-managed allocation; room-wise and person-wise counts, children included. Rules such as two adults per room become validations.

nodes.label: A-2 Payment path (Q2)
nodes.rationale: Default: Phase 1 supports both an online gateway (webhook-driven activation) and offline payment recorded manually by Finance; both create a payments row; subscription activation keys off payments.status = succeeded. AMPM changed: online payment only, by card or UPI, after AMPM creates or invites the account and the client enters basic wedding details; gateway to be selected; manual recording stays as a staff fallback. Offline-only would leave provider/provider_ref unused; online-only disables method = bank_transfer.

nodes.label: A-20 Chat versus tracked questions (Q20)
nodes.rationale: Default: no free-form chat in v1; a client question is a client_requests row of type question with a threaded comments trail, logged and visible to the assigned team. AMPM changed: live chat is required in addition to tracked requests, adding conversations and messages.

nodes.label: A-21 Change requests (Q21)
nodes.rationale: Default: change requests are client_requests of type change_request with the §11 statuses; a configurable threshold marks a request is_material. AMPM confirmed, with a closed status added. A separate table only if the workflow diverges from questions.

nodes.label: A-22 No vendor or hotel logins (Q22)
nodes.norm_label: a-22 no vendor or hotel logins (q22)
nodes.rationale: Default: vendors and hotels never log in; users.user_type has no vendor value. AMPM confirmed. A vendor portal later adds a vendor user type scoped to vendor_assignments; vendors unchanged.

nodes.label: A-23 Post-closure client access (Q23)
nodes.community_name: Wedding Projects, Rooms and Travel Tables
nodes.rationale: Default: clients keep read-only portal access for 12 months after closure (wedding_projects.client_access_until), then the project is archived. AMPM changed: three months of read-only access, then archiving on AMPM approval. The period is configuration.

nodes.label: A-24 Feedback and archive (Q24)
nodes.community_name: Wedding Projects, Rooms and Travel Tables
nodes.rationale: Default: post-wedding feedback is a client_feedback row; archive is wedding_projects.archived_at plus retention jobs. AMPM confirmed feedback form and archived state.

nodes.label: A-25 Material change thresholds (Q25)
nodes.rationale: Default: a change is material when it exceeds configurable thresholds (e.g. a budget line delta of 10 percent or a date or venue change); material changes set is_material and populate impact_flags_json, which drives the SPEC §8 automation. AMPM partly decided: configurable thresholds confirmed; values and approval rules to be defined.

nodes.label: A-3 Plans, trial and demo (Q3)
nodes.rationale: Default: plans supports one-time fixed-term and recurring billing; v1 configured one-time fixed-term with manual renewal; trial is subscription status trial on a plan with trial_days; demo is a plan flagged is_demo on an account flagged is_demo; entitlements come from plan_modules. AMPM confirmed: Rs 50,000, one-time, one month, configurable; renewal is a new purchase; no separate trial plan, the demo serves that purpose. Recurring billing would need subscription_invoices and dunning states; auto_renew and ends_at already exist.

nodes.label: A-4 Margin and client-facing amounts (Q4)
nodes.rationale: Default: AMPM may earn a margin on vendor and hotel pricing, so every commercial record stores client-facing amounts and internal cost in separate columns (vendor_proposals, hotel_proposals, budget_lines, room_blocks, project_final_accounts). Clients see estimates, approved amounts, invoices issued to them, their own payments and outstanding milestones; never vendor quotes, internal cost, margin, vendor invoices or vendor contracts. AMPM partly decided: internal cost and margin never shown confirmed; wedding management fee set outside the app; online milestone payment out of the first release; which client-facing amounts the portal shows still to be confirmed. A transparent fee model would need no structural change.

nodes.label: A-5 Client users per wedding (Q5)
nodes.rationale: Default: several client users per wedding through project_members with project_role client_owner / client_approver / client_viewer; can_view_finance flag; approvals need one decision by default, approvals.required_decisions allows more. AMPM changed: two family representatives, one per side, with equal rights; no viewer role and no finance flag; shared or separate logins to be decided, separate recommended.

nodes.label: A-6 Roles and cost visibility (Q6)
nodes.rationale: Default: the eleven SPEC §6 roles adopted as global staff roles plus external roles (client via project membership, guest via token, demo prospect). Internal cost and margin readable by Super Admin and Finance everywhere, the Wedding Project Manager on assigned projects, the Vendor Coordinator for vendor-side cost and the Hotel team for hotel-side cost. AMPM partly decided: department-based access confirmed; final role list and who may see hotel and vendor costs to be confirmed. Role changes alter roles and role_permissions seed data only.

nodes.label: A-7 Guest list and RSVP model (Q7)
nodes.norm_label: a-7 guest list and rsvp model (q7)
nodes.rationale: Default: guest list loaded first (client upload or AMPM entry); each family group receives a unique tokenised RSVP link; guests respond per person per function; a group may add accompanying members up to family_groups.max_additional_guests (default 0); no open registration; dietary preference for everyone, allergies and accessibility optional and SENSITIVE; client sees own guest list except RESTRICTED and identity fields. AMPM changed: links per side or one combined link (final structure open); guests identify themselves against the loaded list; no editing after submission; corrections through the RSVP team; per-person counting, meal preference and allergies confirmed; family representatives see summaries only and cannot edit the list. A shared wedding link needs self-identification and a de-duplication queue, with rsvp_tokens.family_group_id nullable.

nodes.label: A-8 Identity documents (Q8)
nodes.rationale: Default: collected only when a project enables it for a defined purpose (hotel check-in); Aadhaar numbers never stored; accepted passport, voter ID, driving licence; files in a separate restricted bucket; retention_until defaults to checkout plus 30 days; every read audited. AMPM partly decided: per wedding, no Aadhaar and restricted storage confirmed; automatic deletion removed; retention follows AMPM-approved policy, to be confirmed. If Aadhaar is legally needed, add document_type = aadhaar_masked after legal review.

nodes.label: A-9 Hotel commercials and availability (Q9)
nodes.rationale: Default: indicative rate cards with line items (room rate by category, venue rental, per-plate minimums, taxes), client-visible once verified; negotiated rates in hotel_proposals with client and internal amounts; availability checked manually per enquiry, no calendar; per-asset media rights; hotels bulk-imported through import_jobs. AMPM confirmed and extended: prices are indicative ranges including wedding package ranges and per-plate pricing, menu grids, street view; Eva updates about three times a year; about 200 hotels at the start. A live calendar would add hotel_availability_days.

nodes.label: Coverage against the audit (§20)
nodes.rationale: §20.1 maps the SPEC §3 records that §4 did not model to their new tables. §20.2 maps audit findings GP-1..GP-44 and AM-1..AM-15 to their resolution. Not resolved by a data model: GP-4 recurring billing scope, GP-7 refunds, GP-28 calendar sync, GP-33..GP-40 non-functional and compliance items, GP-42 and GP-43 hosting.

nodes.label: Changes from AMPM's decisions of 25 October 2026 (§0a)
nodes.norm_label: changes from ampm's decisions of 25 october 2026 (§0a)
nodes.rationale: Decisions that changed the model: Q9 indicative price ranges, wedding packages, street view; Q2 couple_names and preferred_locations at activation; Q5 two family representatives; Q7 RSVP link scope, self-identification, locked responses, correction requests; Q20 live chat module Q; Q8/Q17 no automatic deletion; Q23 three-month access window and archived_by; Q4 vendor_assignments.share_contact; Q21 closed status; Q3 call_request activity; Q12 CMS dormant; Q16 GST dormant; Q1 native apps need no table changes.

nodes.label: Entity index with phases and restricted fields (§19)
nodes.norm_label: entity index with phases and restricted fields (§19)
nodes.rationale: Lists every entity with module, phase (per SPEC §11 as adjusted by A-10) and the fields or whole tables the permission matrix guards server-side. Count: 108 tables including join tables, two dormant, against 35 rows in SPEC §4.

nodes.label: Module overview ER diagram (§2)
nodes.rationale: Core entities only: leads convert to client_accounts, which hold subscriptions, service_agreements, saved_hotels, hotel_enquiries and wedding_projects; the wedding project is the parent of functions, budget lines, vendor assignments, designs, approvals, requests, family groups, room blocks, tasks, incidents, invoices and documents.

nodes.label: Open modelling questions for review (§21)
nodes.rationale: 1 client-visible actuals (budget_lines.actual_amount CLIENT by default, Q4); 2 vendor contacts after selection via per-assignment share_contact (Q4, Q22); 3 guest contact details visible to the client even when AMPM adds guests (Q7); 4 one polymorphic comments table versus per-entity tables; 5 real demo hotels with masked rates versus invented sample hotels (A-28); 6 audit granularity for restricted-field reads; 7 monthly partitioning of audit_events and notifications, indexing of guest_function_attendance, revisit if volumes exceed A-15.

nodes.label: Test identifiers AC-nn.m
nodes.rationale: Each test is numbered under the acceptance criterion it proves, so a criterion's coverage is readable from the identifier.

nodes.label: AMBIGUITY finding (AM)
nodes.rationale: A sentence that can be read two ways; the brief says which reading was taken. 15 in the audit, 9 placed; the other six are modelling detail answered in the data model.

nodes.label: CONFLICT finding (CF)
nodes.rationale: Two of AMPM's documents say different things; AMPM chooses which stands. All nine are placed in the brief.

nodes.label: COVERED requirement
nodes.rationale: A requirement the design meets as written, marked so AMPM can see what needs no discussion.

nodes.label: DECISION question (Q)
nodes.rationale: A question only AMPM can answer; all 25 are placed in the brief and listed with choices in the open decisions document.

nodes.label: GAP finding (GP)
nodes.rationale: Something the platform needs that no document specifies; each names its audit identifier and says how the design fills it meanwhile. 44 in the audit, 38 placed in the brief, 6 purely technical ones in the architecture plan.

nodes.label: Where each question came from, and the repeats (R to Q and draft traceability)
nodes.norm_label: where each question came from, and the repeats (r to q and draft traceability)
nodes.rationale: Maps every R question to AMPM's eleven brief items, the developer's Q number, the draft sections that also ask it, and whether AMPM's own documents already answer it — so the same question is never asked twice. Records the merges: AMPM items 1 and 2 are one question (R1), item 9 covers Q8 and Q17 (R12), and item 3 is half answered by the brief's own section 3. R3, R4, R6, R7, R8, R10, R11, R16 and R17 were on no AMPM list; they come from the business explanation, the specification or the decision log. Also notes that the drafts' review sections still list questions the 25 October answers settled, which will be removed at the next revision.

nodes.label: R15: WhatsApp, SMS and email providers and account ownership
nodes.norm_label: r15: whatsapp, sms and email providers and account ownership
nodes.rationale: WhatsApp Business onboarding and Indian SMS registration (DLT) take two to six weeks and must be done in AMPM's name, so they start before coding; because clients sign in by OTP, the SMS provider is a launch dependency. The brief proposes email, WhatsApp and SMS as channels with provider selection to be confirmed. Assumed: WhatsApp through the WhatsApp Business Platform via an Indian business solution provider, email through Amazon SES, SMS through a DLT-registered Indian provider for OTP and as a fallback, all three behind one adapter so a later swap is contained. Proposal: the developer selects the business solution provider and the SMS provider on price and reliability while AMPM owns the accounts, and AMPM creates its Meta Business Manager and registers the sender for DLT in the first week. Deferring WhatsApp removes the longest lead time but leaves only email and SMS at launch.

nodes.label: AC-01 Public enquiry saves source and owner; team tracks follow-up
nodes.norm_label: ac-01 public enquiry saves source and owner; team tracks follow-up
nodes.rationale: Duplicate leads are flagged, never refused or auto-merged; a converted lead becomes read-only and the only path to an account is an invitation.

nodes.label: AC-02 Subscription activates hotel discovery without exposing full wedding modules
nodes.norm_label: ac-02 subscription activates hotel discovery without exposing full wedding modules
nodes.rationale: Online purchase, manual bank transfer and renewal all activate exactly the plan's modules; expiry removes modules and nothing else; the trial test AC-02.8 is dormant because the demo serves as the trial (Q3); no self-registration route exists.

nodes.label: AC-02.11 Renewal restores access and preserves data
nodes.norm_label: ac-02.11 renewal restores access and preserves data
nodes.rationale: Nothing is deleted on expiry, so a new subscription makes the six saved hotels and both enquiries reachable again with their history (Q3).

nodes.label: AC-03 Demo account cannot access records outside demo scope
nodes.norm_label: ac-03 demo account cannot access records outside demo scope
nodes.rationale: Demo data lives in the same database behind flags (V-10); rates are masked, non-demo hotels are 404, demo rows are invisible to operational staff and demo users cannot export.

nodes.label: AC-04 Hotel search shows freshness of pricing; unverified availability is never shown as confirmed
nodes.norm_label: ac-04 hotel search shows freshness of pricing; unverified availability is never shown as confirmed
nodes.rationale: Verified, stale and unverified cards carry distinct labels; the word 'confirmed' must not appear in rate context; availability is labelled separately from rates and answered inside an enquiry.

nodes.label: AC-05 AMPM records negotiation and site visit without exposing internal notes
nodes.norm_label: ac-05 ampm records negotiation and site visit without exposing internal notes
nodes.rationale: Internal-only events, restricted enquiry fields and hotel contacts never serialise to clients; 'preview as client' must be byte-identical to the real client response; an enquiry is not a confirmed booking until a done confirmed milestone and a signed contract exist; chargeable services wait for an active agreement.

nodes.label: AC-06 Engaged client receives correct project and permissions
nodes.norm_label: ac-06 engaged client receives correct project and permissions
nodes.rationale: Project creation needs only minimal fields and back-fills saved hotels, enquiry and agreement; client roles and the finance flag shape the portal with no placeholder for missing regions; membership removal ends access immediately; on-behalf decisions need evidence and a badge (V-14).

nodes.label: AC-07 Multiple functions have independent vendors, schedules, budgets and approvals
nodes.norm_label: ac-07 multiple functions have independent vendors, schedules, budgets and approvals
nodes.rationale: Approving one function's proposal leaves the other untouched; cancelling a function keeps its records (soft delete).

nodes.label: AC-08 Vendor shortlist permits fewer than five options; it does not require exactly ten
nodes.norm_label: ac-08 vendor shortlist permits fewer than five options; it does not require exactly ten
nodes.rationale: SPEC 1.2 says 'aiming for 5 to 10' but two options and twelve options must both present cleanly; availability conflicts warn but do not block.

nodes.label: AC-09 Approval refers to the exact design, menu or proposal version; revisions do not overwrite it
nodes.norm_label: ac-09 approval refers to the exact design, menu or proposal version; revisions do not overwrite it
nodes.rationale: A new version supersedes and the old one is immutable; approval locks the version and budget line; menu approval freezes the guaranteed headcount; approving an invitation does not send it.

nodes.label: AC-10 Self-service and AMPM-assisted RSVP update the same guest database without duplicates
nodes.norm_label: ac-10 self-service and ampm-assisted rsvp update the same guest database without duplicates
nodes.rationale: Both paths upsert the same guest_function_attendance rows and add rsvp_responses snapshots; per-side links identify the household (Q7); submitted responses are locked and corrections go through the RSVP team; allergies are sensitive; identity capture is conditional and audited.

nodes.label: AC-10.11 Side link: a guest identifies their household
nodes.norm_label: ac-10.11 side link: a guest identifies their household
nodes.rationale: An exact match opens the household's RSVP; a near match is held for RSVP-team review; no household data is shown before a confirmed match; a groom-side household cannot be found through the bride-side link (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-10.12 Unmatched guests are held for review
nodes.norm_label: ac-10.12 unmatched guests are held for review
nodes.rationale: A pending household with identification_status review counts for nothing until the RSVP team approves (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-10.13 Submitted responses are locked; corrections go through the team
nodes.norm_label: ac-10.13 submitted responses are locked; corrections go through the team
nodes.rationale: The reopened link shows a read-only summary; a correction request creates a guest_support_requests row and RG's change writes the same attendance rows with response_source ampm_call (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-11 Attendance changes update totals and flag downstream planning impacts
nodes.norm_label: ac-11 attendance changes update totals and flag downstream planning impacts
nodes.rationale: Recalculation changes expected_count but never guaranteed_count; rooming and transfer changes are flagged and logistics notified once; recalculation is idempotent.

nodes.label: AC-12 Unauthorised users cannot access restricted data by changing URLs, API requests or file links
nodes.norm_label: ac-12 unauthorised users cannot access restricted data by changing urls, api requests or file links
nodes.rationale: A generated suite covers every resource, principal and action; identifier tampering returns 404 with bodies and timing identical to a nonexistent id; signed file links expire and bind to one file; break-glass reads by SA are audited and alerted.

nodes.label: AC-13 Production readiness cannot be completed without required checks or an authorised exception
nodes.norm_label: ac-13 production readiness cannot be completed without required checks or an authorised exception
nodes.rationale: Readiness derives automatically from required items; exceptions may only be authorised by SA (Q10), PM and HL attempts return 403.

nodes.label: AC-14 Incidents can be assigned, escalated and closed with resolution notes
nodes.norm_label: ac-14 incidents can be assigned, escalated and closed with resolution notes
nodes.rationale: Critical incidents escalate automatically along the configured chain; critical resolution requires notes; client visibility is off by default and never exposes description or notes.

nodes.label: AC-15 Closure checks departure, lost-and-found, vendor completion and financial reconciliation
nodes.norm_label: ac-15 closure checks departure, lost-and-found, vendor completion and financial reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Each closure item verifies against data (409 until satisfied); closing deletes nothing; client access ends after the configured window and only SA may reopen; retention after closure requires SA approval (Q17).

nodes.label: AC-16 Responsive and accessible interfaces
nodes.rationale: Key screens render at 1280, 1024 and 375 px; WCAG 2.1 AA via axe-core; the guest wizard gets a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass.

nodes.label: AC-17 Secure authentication
nodes.rationale: Staff must enrol an authenticator before first use; clients and prospects sign in by mobile OTP (Q13); lockout with generic errors; single-use time-boxed tokens; Argon2id password storage; guest sessions bound to the household token.

nodes.label: AC-17.9 Mobile OTP sign-in for prospects and clients
nodes.norm_label: ac-17.9 mobile otp sign-in for prospects and clients
nodes.rationale: Codes are single use and expire in ten minutes; an uninvited number receives a neutral message and no session (Q13).

nodes.label: AC-18 Server-side validation on every protected request
nodes.norm_label: ac-18 server-side validation on every protected request
nodes.rationale: Validations are generated from field-matrix.csv; required-at-stage rules return 409; mass assignment of internal_cost, is_demo or status is never applied; uniqueness returns 409.

nodes.label: AC-19 Encryption in transit and at rest
nodes.norm_label: ac-19 encryption in transit and at rest
nodes.rationale: TLS 1.2+ with HSTS; three customer-managed keys with the restricted bucket on its own key; no secrets in code, images or logs.

nodes.label: AC-20 Private file storage, expiring links and safe uploads
nodes.norm_label: ac-20 private file storage, expiring links and safe uploads
nodes.rationale: Content-type detection, size limits, antivirus scan, image metadata stripping; document access follows the owning record's visibility.

nodes.label: AC-21 Audit trail
nodes.rationale: Every listed action writes one event with actor, entity, before and after; audit_events is append-only at the database level and partitioned monthly; viewer scope follows roles.

nodes.label: AC-22 Backups and tested restoration
nodes.rationale: Point-in-time restore drill within 4 hours and 15 minutes of data (RPO/RTO measured, not assumed, V-13); object storage restore from versions and replica region; backup failure alerts.

nodes.label: AC-23 Search, filters, pagination and bulk operations
nodes.norm_label: ac-23 search, filters, pagination and bulk operations
nodes.rationale: Keyset pagination at 50 per page with no duplicates or gaps; bulk operations run as one job with one audit event per changed row; trigram hotel search relevance.

nodes.label: AC-24 Media optimisation and controlled video delivery
nodes.norm_label: ac-24 media optimisation and controlled video delivery
nodes.rationale: Derivatives generated by job; video transcoded and served only with expiring signed tokens; rights status gates client and public visibility.

nodes.label: AC-25 Configurable packages, categories, statuses and pricing
nodes.norm_label: ac-25 configurable packages, categories, statuses and pricing
nodes.rationale: Reference data edits take effect without a deploy; thresholds drive automation; a CI static check fails the build on any commercial literal in code (BIZ rule 8).

nodes.label: AC-26 Clear errors, duplicate-submission prevention and form recovery
nodes.norm_label: ac-26 clear errors, duplicate-submission prevention and form recovery
nodes.rationale: Double submission creates one record via idempotency keys; drafts survive refresh; errors name the field, keep input and are announced to assistive technology.

nodes.label: AC-27 Retention, deletion and privacy
nodes.rationale: Consent is captured with its notice version; data principal export and erasure anonymise personal fields but keep attendance counts; retention deletes only after SA approval; logs contain no personal data.

nodes.label: AC-28 Integration boundaries
nodes.rationale: Adapters are contract-tested against sandboxes; card data never leaves AMPM; provider outages retry with backoff and dead-letter; payloads carry only the fields listed in architecture section 10.

nodes.label: AC-29 Notifications and automation
nodes.rationale: Approval requests go to CO and approvers with can_approve, never CV; material changes create review tasks; the notification log is complete; preferences and opt-in are honoured.

nodes.label: AC-30 Reports and exports
nodes.rationale: Every SPEC section 9 report computes from the seed; permissions follow permission-matrix section 5.16; the rooming list export for hotels carries names, dates and room category only.

nodes.label: AC-31 Status transitions and guards
nodes.rationale: Transition tests are generated from permission-matrix section 7: unlisted principals get 403, unlisted transitions get 409 with the guard message; status labels are display only.

nodes.label: AC-32 Entitlement resolution and downgrades
nodes.rationale: Each account state yields exactly the documented module set; downgrade is read-only before removal; the entitlement cache is invalidated on write, not only on expiry.

nodes.label: AC-33 Offline behaviour on event day
nodes.norm_label: ac-33 offline behaviour on event day
nodes.rationale: Read caches with an 'offline since' indicator; queued mutations sync in order with original timestamps; server status wins conflicts and the offline change is logged; local data is encrypted and wiped on sign-out (first release on native builds, Q1).

nodes.label: AC-33.5 Local data is protected on native builds
nodes.norm_label: ac-33.5 local data is protected on native builds
nodes.rationale: The local store is encrypted at rest, holds only the user's role-scoped data and is wiped on sign-out (Q1).

nodes.label: AC-33.6 Offline state and pending changes are visible
nodes.norm_label: ac-33.6 offline state and pending changes are visible
nodes.rationale: An offline banner shows the pending-change count, which drains to zero on reconnect with each change keeping its original time (Q1).

nodes.label: AC-34 Performance and capacity
nodes.rationale: k6 profiles for hotel search, RSVP burst, team workspace mixed load and job throughput; profiles rescaled to 200 hotels and 20 weddings (Q15).

nodes.label: AC-35 Imports
nodes.rationale: Hotel and guest imports validate first and apply with audit per row; duplicates by phone are flagged, not merged; identity columns are refused, allergies only through the sensitive mapping step.

nodes.label: AC-36 Finance integrity
nodes.rationale: Client and internal amounts never mix (schema assertion); approved amounts are locked except for an audited FA override; GST invoice tests AC-36.3 and AC-36.4 are dormant (Q16); refunds cannot exceed the original payment.

nodes.label: AC-37 Live chat alongside tracked requests
nodes.norm_label: ac-37 live chat alongside tracked requests
nodes.rationale: Conversations reach staff within two seconds and can become tracked client_requests; chat never carries an approval; conversations are isolated per account; unanswered conversations surface to the department lead (Q20).

nodes.label: AC-38 Department-based access
nodes.rationale: Each department sees only the resources permission-matrix section 5 grants; project membership bounds every department; cost visibility is limited to roles AMPM still has to finalise (Q6).

nodes.label: Denial semantics: 404 for invisible records, 403 for forbidden actions, 400 for validation, 409 for transition guards
nodes.norm_label: denial semantics: 404 for invisible records, 403 for forbidden actions, 400 for validation, 409 for transition guards
nodes.rationale: A principal that may not see a record receives 404 with the same body as for a nonexistent record so existence cannot be inferred; a visible record with a forbidden action gets 403; validation failures return 400 naming the field; status-transition violations return 409 with the guard message. Tests assert these codes exactly.

nodes.label: Idempotency of jobs, webhooks and submissions
nodes.norm_label: idempotency of jobs, webhooks and submissions

nodes.label: Schema assertion over client-facing responses (additional properties forbidden)
nodes.norm_label: schema assertion over client-facing responses (additional properties forbidden)
nodes.rationale: Finance-leak and restricted-field tests compare every client-facing response against the serialiser schema rather than spot checks (V-8); sentinel values are seeded into every restricted, sensitive, secret and bank field and must never appear in any CO, CA, CV, GU or DP body.

Decision: Guest invitation links are issued per side (one for the bride's side, one for the groom's side) or as one combined link when AMPM chooses; the final structure is to be decided. The RSVP team imports or creates the guest list and sends the links. Guests cannot see other households or the guest list, and cannot edit a submitted response; corrections go through a change request or the help option to the RSVP caller. The two family representatives see approved RSVP summaries and cannot edit the list. Each guest is counted individually, children included; meal preference, allergies where required, rooming and travel where applicable are collected. Open: Final link structure: per side, or one combined link.

nodes.rationale: Groups R4 to R8: what clients can reach (browser as well as apps), who they are (one shared login or two accounts), how a decision is completed (one approval or both), what money they see, and which hotel services carry a fee. These five decide the client-facing surface and therefore the largest open cost item in the estimate.

nodes.label: Group 3: Your team (roles, cost visibility, staff sign-in)
nodes.norm_label: group 3: your team (roles, cost visibility, staff sign-in)
nodes.rationale: Groups R9 and R10 because both are about internal access: every screen, permission and test in the drafts is built on the staff role list, and staff accounts reach costs and identity documents, so they need stronger authentication than a client account.

nodes.label: Group 4: Guests (RSVP link structure)
nodes.rationale: Holds the single guest-facing open point (R11): the link style decides the first screen of the RSVP form, how duplicates are prevented, and which drafted tests run.

nodes.label: Group 5: Privacy and retention
nodes.rationale: Holds R12. AMPM's Q8 and Q17 answers both point at one decision — retention periods plus privacy wording — which is why AMPM's item 9 and the developer's Q8 and Q17 are treated as the same question.

nodes.label: Group 7: Changes and the end of a wedding
nodes.norm_label: group 7: changes and the end of a wedding
nodes.rationale: Groups R18 and R19: the two workflow rules at the end of a project's life — when a change counts as material and who approves it, and who approves archiving and how access is restored later. Both are rules inside flows that are already built, so only the named approver and the threshold values are missing.

nodes.label: R10: How staff sign in
nodes.rationale: Clients sign in by mobile number and OTP, as decided, but the brief's section 13 defers the staff method to the development team. Staff accounts reach costs, identity documents and every wedding they are assigned to, so they need stronger protection, and staff work inside venues with poor signal where an SMS code may not arrive. Proposal: email, password and a six-digit authenticator-app code, which works without network on the wedding day. Alternatives: password plus SMS OTP, which makes the SMS provider a wedding-day dependency for the team app; or sign-in through Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 if AMPM uses one, which gives central control when someone leaves but needs the workspace account details.

nodes.label: R11: RSVP link structure — per side, combined, or household links
nodes.norm_label: r11: rsvp link structure — per side, combined, or household links
nodes.rationale: The brief requires separate bride's-side and groom's-side links and allows one combined link where AMPM chooses to use it; the compiled answers say the final link structure is to be decided. The choice decides the first screen of the RSVP form, how duplicates are prevented, and which drafted tests run: with per-side or combined links a guest must find themselves in the loaded list before responding, while a private link per household removes that step but needs a phone number or email for every household up front. Proposal: per-side links as the standard and the combined link as a per-wedding option, both in the first release since they share one mechanism, keeping household links available for weddings whose list arrives with contacts.

nodes.label: R12: Retention periods and privacy wording
nodes.norm_label: r12: retention periods and privacy wording
nodes.rationale: AMPM's answers say nothing is deleted automatically and that AMPM approves retention and deletion, so the system needs the periods after which it proposes a deletion for approval, and the enquiry and RSVP forms need agreed privacy notices before launch. AMPM's Q8 and Q17 answers point at this one decision, which is why AMPM's item 9 and the developer's Q8 and Q17 are merged here. Assumed periods: closed leads 24 months; guest personal data 12 months after the wedding project closes; identity documents 30 days after checkout; demo data reset on a schedule. When a period ends the system lists the records and a Super Admin approves — nothing is deleted unattended — and notices are designed to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023. Periods are settings; wording supplied by AMPM instead of drafted by the developer shortens Phase 3 by a few days.

nodes.label: R14: Capacity — staff, weddings, guests, hotels and media
nodes.norm_label: r14: capacity — staff, weddings, guests, hotels and media
nodes.rationale: The numbers size the database, the storage and the load tests, and they go into the cost estimate. AMPM's answer gives two of the four — about 200 hotels and about 20 concurrent weddings — while the brief asks that staff and guest capacity be confirmed before implementation; the business explanation's worked example is a 250-guest wedding in Jaipur. The drafts were originally sized for 50 staff, 40 concurrent weddings, 1,500 guests per wedding, 500 hotels and 2 TB of media in the first year, and are now rescaled to 200 hotels and 20 weddings with staff and guests unchanged. Proposal: confirm 50 staff accounts and 1,500 guests as upper bounds. Larger numbers change indexing and the storage estimate, not the design.

nodes.label: R17: One go-live, or hotel discovery first
nodes.norm_label: r17: one go-live, or hotel discovery first
nodes.rationale: Raised by the developer and the decision that shapes the schedule more than any other open point, which is why the schedule and cost estimate wait on it. Hotel discovery is the product sold by subscription and is complete at the end of Phase 1, while the wedding modules take three more phases: launching discovery first brings subscriptions in months earlier and lets real prospects test the demo, at the price of two go-lives and support starting earlier. AMPM's documents give the first release's content but never say whether it is one date or two. The drafts currently gate one launch at the end of Phase 4 with discovery-first noted as the open alternative. Proposal: option B, discovery live at the end of Phase 1 and the wedding modules as one second go-live, so the first wedding managed in the system is one whose discovery happened in it. B and C add a stabilisation pass and a support window per go-live; A delays the first subscription to the end of Phase 4.

nodes.label: R18: Material-change thresholds and who approves a material change
nodes.norm_label: r18: material-change thresholds and who approves a material change
nodes.rationale: Material changes trigger review tasks and notifications, so too low a threshold floods the team and too high a one lets a large change through unnoticed; the thresholds are configurable as AMPM asked but need starting values, and the approval rule is a workflow to build. AMPM's Q25 answer says the definition is not finalised and that budget-change percentages, date and venue thresholds will be decided by AMPM. Assumed: material when a budget line moves 10 percent or more, or a function's date or venue changes, raising impact flags and review tasks for the affected teams, with the client's approval following the normal approval rule (R6). Proposal adds 5 percent of the total approved budget, and a second approver — Super Admin or senior management — above roughly 15 percent of the total budget. Values are settings; a second approver adds a step and a waiting state to the change-request flow.

nodes.label: R19: Archiving a wedding and restoring access later
nodes.norm_label: r19: archiving a wedding and restoring access later
nodes.rationale: DECIDED in substance: the brief's section 11 already sets read-only client access for three months after the wedding, then archiving on AMPM's approval, with records not automatically deleted, later access controlled by AMPM, and archiving defined as a change of status and permissions rather than deletion. Only the mechanics are missing, because the three-month window and the archive are built but the approval step and the reopening path need a named person and a rule. Assumed: a reminder to the representatives before the window ends; the Project Manager proposes archiving and the Super Admin approves; client memberships are removed so the representatives can still sign in and see a contact route but no project; archived weddings stay readable to authorised staff and are excluded from day-to-day lists. Proposal adds the reopening rule: a representative asks AMPM, the Super Admin restores read-only access for 30 days with a logged reason, editing never reopens, and later corrections are made by staff with a note. All of these are rules inside one flow; none changes the data.

nodes.label: R2: Payment gateway provider for the Rs 50,000 subscription
nodes.norm_label: r2: payment gateway provider for the rs 50,000 subscription
nodes.rationale: Only the provider is open: the brief's section 3 already settles the transaction-handling requirements (payment record; amount, date, status and transaction reference; activation after confirmation; no duplicate activation from repeated notifications; start and expiry dates; staff review of payment status) and all of it is in the drafts. The merchant account takes one to two weeks to open and must be in AMPM's name, and the gateway code is written in Phase 1. Proposal: Razorpay with hosted checkout and activation driven by the gateway's notification, unless AMPM already has a merchant account elsewhere; PayU and Cashfree fit the same adapter, so a swap is a few days of work as long as card, UPI and payment notifications are supported.

nodes.label: R4: Client portals in the browser as well as in the apps
nodes.norm_label: r4: client portals in the browser as well as in the apps
nodes.rationale: Raised by the developer, not on AMPM's list, and the largest open cost item. Families compare hotels with photographs, menus and price grids, which many prefer on a laptop; the demo is reached from the website; app-only means every prospect installs an app before seeing the demo. Against that, a web version is a further build to design, test and maintain. Both AMPM documents can be true at once: the original specification asked for a responsive desktop, tablet and mobile interface, while the brief asks for iOS and Android and leaves the final architecture to be agreed. Proposal: option B, the discovery and wedding portals also run in the browser, built from the same code as the client app so screens are designed once; the team app stays native because of offline wedding-day use. Option C removes the client app and its app-store work; option A is cheapest but costs the laptop experience and adds an install step before the demo.

nodes.label: R5: Two representative accounts or one shared login
nodes.norm_label: r5: two representative accounts or one shared login
nodes.rationale: CONFLICT between AMPM's two documents of 25 October: the compiled questions and answers say under Q5 that both representatives will use the same login credentials, while the brief's section 5 says the choice must be finalised before development and that separate authenticated accounts are preferable for security and audit history. The brief's position is the later and more considered one and matches the developer's recommendation. With one shared login the system cannot tell who approved a design, menu or budget line — the audit trail says only 'the client' — and one phone number has to receive both families' OTPs. Proposal: two accounts with identical rights on the same wedding; they still share responsibility, they just do not share a phone.

nodes.label: R6: Does one representative's approval complete a decision, or must both approve
nodes.norm_label: r6: does one representative's approval complete a decision, or must both approve
nodes.rationale: The specification's section 13 lists whether multiple approvals are required among the decisions to confirm, and the 25 October answers settle who is authorised but not how many. One approval keeps things moving; two protect both families on money matters but add a step to every approval screen plus a wait whenever one representative is unavailable. Proposal: one approval for everything in the first release, with the number as a setting per approval type so budgets and contracts can later require two while designs and menus require one. Two approvals add a 'waiting for the other side' state and a reminder to the second representative.

nodes.label: R7: Which amounts the client sees in the wedding portal
nodes.norm_label: r7: which amounts the client sees in the wedding portal
nodes.rationale: Raised by the developer. AMPM's rule on what must never be shown is clear (internal costs, margins, vendor rates, quotations, negotiations); what is shown is not, yet both the business explanation and the specification ask for a client-facing budget and the specification lists financial visibility among the decisions to confirm, so those screens cannot be signed off. Since milestone payments are not collected online in the first release, the amounts are shown for information only. Three levels: level 1 planned budget and approved amounts per function; level 2 adds invoices issued to the client and payment status; level 3 adds actual spend and variance per line. The drafts currently show level 3; the proposal is level 2, keeping actual spend and variance internal. Level 1 removes the invoices and payments screens from the client portal for now. Separately, hotel booking-milestone amounts are assumed visible only where the client pays the hotel directly.

nodes.label: R9: Staff roles, and who may see hotel costs and vendor costs
nodes.norm_label: r9: staff roles, and who may see hotel costs and vendor costs
nodes.rationale: Every screen, permission and test in the drafts is built on the role list, so it has to be final: the brief names departments only as functional examples and says the final list must follow AMPM's approved staff structure, while cost visibility is the one permission the brief singles out as restricted to specifically authorised personnel. Assumed nine roles from the specification: Super Admin; Sales / Relationship Manager; Hotel / Destination Team; Wedding Project Manager; Creative / Design Team; Vendor Coordinator; RSVP / Guest Team; Hospitality / Logistics Team; Finance / Accounts. Hotel costs visible to Super Admin, Finance and the Hotel Team; vendor costs to Super Admin, Finance and the Vendor Coordinator; the Project Manager sees both for their own weddings; everyone else sees client-facing amounts only. Adding or renaming a role is a day of work; moving cost visibility is a permission change plus a test change. Open sub-point: whether 'senior authorised management' needs a role of its own or is the Super Admin role.

nodes.label: Short answers and defaults to tick
nodes.norm_label: short answers and defaults to tick
nodes.rationale: Eight small defaults that a tick keeps and a line changes: accounting-software export for Finance (CSV by default, since the platform issues no GST invoices); privacy-respecting analytics on public pages plus a bot check on enquiry and demo forms; who at AMPM signs each phase's acceptance on staging; emergency reading of identity documents by the Super Admin, audited each time; RSVP reminder cadence then a call from the RSVP team, with no guest edits after the deadline; readiness checklists hidden from the client; programme and calendar files for guests once invitations go out; one subscription per client account rather than per wedding.

nodes.norm_label: r4: web as well as apps

nodes.norm_label: r8: hotel services with a fee

Options: agree / changes ___.

nodes.label: MemPalace global shell hooks caveat
nodes.rationale: MemPalace's own shell hooks (mempal_save_hook.sh, mempal_precompact_hook.sh in ~/.claude/settings.json) file a running session's transcript under the shared wing wing_api without naming the project; because MemPalace keys drawers by content and upserts, they overwrite the wing the project hooks set. Fix: point them at the project-aware runner (mempalace hook run --hook stop --harness claude-code, and --hook precompact) and re-key the shared wing with mempalace wings split --wing wing_api (plan, then --yes, then mempalace hallways --rebuild). Done on the development Mac on 26 October 2026.

nodes.label: Principle: commercial rules are configuration
nodes.rationale: Plans, packages, categories, thresholds, templates and labels are database rows editable by the Super Admin (SPEC §10 avoid hard-coded commercial rules).

nodes.label: Principle: integrations behind adapters
nodes.rationale: Payment, messaging, email, video and maps are each one interface with one provider implementation so a provider change never touches business logic.

nodes.label: Principle: managed, boring infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Managed PostgreSQL, object storage, queues and containers; infrastructure as code; nothing hand-built on a server.

nodes.label: Principle: modular monolith, not microservices
nodes.rationale: At T-7 scale one deployable API and one worker are simpler, cheaper and easier for a small team; module boundaries follow the data model so a later split is a deployment change, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Principle: everything important is versioned, audited and recoverable
nodes.norm_label: principle: everything important is versioned, audited and recoverable

nodes.label: AUTH-01 Sign in
nodes.rationale: Generic invalid-credentials message, no hint which part failed, no registration link and no indication whether an email exists. After Q13 this screen (email, password, authenticator code) is for staff only.

nodes.label: AUTH-02 Account activation
nodes.rationale: Turns a single-use 7-day invitation token into an active login; after Q13 activation ends in OTP sign-in for clients.

nodes.label: AUTH-03 Password reset
nodes.rationale: Neutral confirmation regardless of whether the email exists; 1-hour token; resets revoke other sessions; staff only after Q13.

nodes.label: AUTH-04 Access help
nodes.rationale: The flowchart's Contact AMPM for access help: a minimal form that creates a Sales task, creates no account and reveals nothing about existing accounts.

nodes.label: AUTH-05 Authenticator enrolment (staff)
nodes.rationale: Mandatory second factor before first staff use (A-13); cannot be skipped; recovery codes shown once and stored hashed.

nodes.label: AUTH-06 Mobile OTP sign-in (prospects and clients)
nodes.norm_label: auth-06 mobile otp sign-in (prospects and clients)
nodes.rationale: Added for AMPM's Q13 decision: mobile number with country code (default +91), six-digit code with 10-minute single-use expiry, resend after countdown, remember this device, consent on first sign-in. No registration: a number AMPM has not invited or authorised never gets in; an unknown number gets a neutral message and a lead activity if it matches a lead. Codes go by SMS with WhatsApp fallback (T-6 changed).

nodes.label: Authentication screens AUTH (sign-in, activation, recovery, OTP)
nodes.norm_label: authentication screens auth (sign-in, activation, recovery, otp)
nodes.rationale: Shared by clients, staff and demo users. No registration screen anywhere: a number or email AMPM has not invited never gets in (WHY section 4). After AMPM's Q13 decision, AUTH-01 email/password/authenticator is for staff only and AUTH-06 mobile OTP serves prospects and clients.

nodes.label: CP-40 Feedback
nodes.rationale: Post-wedding feedback once per project after closure (A-24): rating, comments, consent to publish an excerpt.

nodes.label: GR-01 Invitation landing
nodes.rationale: Exchanges the token for a guest session and records consent and notice version; nothing is shown before the token is validated and no other household is ever named. After Q7 it becomes the per-side link with household self-identification.

nodes.label: GR-02 Confirm your household
nodes.rationale: Add a member only while the household's allowance remains, capped server-side (A-7); when exhausted the add button is absent, not disabled; members cannot be removed but can be marked not attending.

nodes.label: GR-04 Meals and needs
nodes.rationale: Dietary preference required for attending members (BIZ rule 7); allergies and accessibility needs are SENSITIVE-GUEST and never shown back outside the permitted classes (GP-24).

nodes.label: GR-05 Travel and accommodation
nodes.rationale: Skipped entirely when the project does not request travel information (TW-33 setting); identity document block only when enabled, with purpose text and retention statement; Aadhaar numbers are refused on upload (A-8, GP-41); files go to the restricted bucket and the guest sees only received.

nodes.label: GR-06 Review and submit
nodes.rationale: Writes attendance, guests, travel segments and the rsvp_responses payload in one atomic transaction (flow 7); submit is idempotent per token and draft version; a failure keeps the draft.

nodes.label: GR-07 Confirmation
nodes.rationale: Attendance summary, hospitality contact, calendar file. After Q7 loses Update your response and gains Request a correction (GR-09, type correction).

nodes.label: GR-08 Link unavailable
nodes.rationale: Explains an expired, revoked or unknown link without revealing data (P-4): no wedding, household or guest data beyond the project name for expired links; a small form creates a reissue task for the RSVP team.

nodes.label: GR-09 Support request
nodes.rationale: Guest help with travel, rooms, meals or access needs; dietary, accessibility and complaint types are treated as sensitive on the staff side.

nodes.label: Guest RSVP portal (GR screens, Phase 3)
nodes.rationale: Mobile-first single-column wizard reached only through a tokenised per-household link; no sign-in, no navigation, language switch, consent notice on the first step, autosave per step (W-6, A-7, P-4). Every screen names the wedding and the responding household so a forwarded link is obviously someone else's; other households and counts are never shown. Prefix GR rather than GP to avoid clashing with the audit's gap identifiers.

nodes.label: PUB-08 Privacy notice and terms
nodes.rationale: Versioned legal pages; the version shown at consent time is recorded on leads.consent_at and guest consent (GP-40).

nodes.label: T3 Form or wizard template
nodes.rationale: Single column, grouped sections, inline validation, sticky footer with Save or Next and Cancel; wizards show a step indicator; drafts autosave.

nodes.label: TW-33 Project settings and members
nodes.rationale: Facts, membership, client access window after closure, and the guest-data switches: identity capture enabled with purpose text, travel information requested (yes, no, by tier).

nodes.label: TW-95 Configuration
nodes.rationale: Thresholds and rules: verification age, material-change thresholds, escalation chain, reminder cadence, retention periods, client access window, demo reset schedule, upload limits, identity capture default. After Q8/Q17 gains a Retention proposals tab where the Super Admin approves deletions proposed by the retention job.

nodes.label: AMPM Platform Wireframe Specifications (wireframes.md v0.2)
nodes.rationale: Draft v0.2 of 25 Oct 2026. A wireframe specification, not a visual design: for every screen it fixes purpose, audience, layout regions, content, actions, states and rules, with low-fidelity sketches. Written because BIZ section 6 requires AMPM to review and approve the exact screen structure before development; extends SPEC section 14, SPEC section 2, BIZ sections 6 and 8 and the two Level-1 flowcharts. Visual design (colour, type, spacing, imagery) is left to AMPM per SPEC.

nodes.label: Double-submission guard and draft recovery
nodes.rationale: Every form guards against double submission and recovers a draft after a refresh; errors keep user input and name the field (SPEC section 10). GR-06 submission is idempotent per token and draft version and atomic.

nodes.label: Modelling conventions (§1)
nodes.rationale: Keys, standard columns, money, statuses, reference tables, versioned records, visibility, polymorphic references, audit, demo isolation and time conventions that apply to every table and are not repeated in the diagrams.

nodes.label: design_items
nodes.rationale: Versioned creative work. function_id nullable; category concept/moodboard/render/invitation/save_the_date/stationery/signage/other; title CLIENT; brief_text (the design brief); status briefing/in_progress/review/approved/archived; owner_user_id; client_visible.

nodes.label: design_versions
nodes.rationale: Design versions, immutable once shared. version_number; summary CLIENT; status draft/shared/revision_requested/approved/rejected/superseded; shared_at; approval_id.

nodes.label: document_access_links
nodes.rationale: Short-lived signed download links, never permanent paths (SPEC §10, §12). token_hash RESTRICTED; expires_at; max_downloads; download_count; created_by; revoked_at.

nodes.label: documents
nodes.rationale: Files with versions. project_id and account_id nullable; owner_type/owner_id (the record the file belongs to); document_type proposal/contract/invoice/design/menu/schedule/rooming_list/rider/ticket/consent/other; storage_key RESTRICTED in private object storage; mime_type; size_bytes; checksum; version_number and previous_version_id (self-reference supersedes); visibility internal/client/guest/public; uploaded_by; retention_class and retention_until (A-17).

nodes.label: hotel_wedding_references
nodes.rationale: Past weddings at the hotel. project_id nullable (the AMPM wedding it refers to); event_year; guest_count; description_client CLIENT; client_visible; consent_document_id from the referenced client (GP-20).

nodes.label: identity_documents
nodes.rationale: Conditional identity capture (A-8, GP-41). document_type passport/voter_id/driving_licence/other, Aadhaar excluded; masked_reference last four characters only; issuing_country; expiry_date; file_document_id stored in the restricted bucket; purpose hotel_checkin/visa/travel; consent_at; collected_by null when uploaded by the guest; retention_until nullable, set only when AMPM approves deletion (Q8, Q17); deletion_approved_by. Never in exports; every read is a restricted_read audit event.

nodes.label: media_assets
nodes.rationale: Images and videos with rights. owner_type hotel/destination/vendor/design_version/invitation_version/project/cms; kind image/video; storage_key RESTRICTED; thumbnail_key; caption; sort_order; visibility internal/client/demo/public; rights_status owned/licensed/consent_required/consent_obtained (GP-20); consent_source_project_id (the wedding the media came from); consent_document_id; uploaded_by. Hotel galleries and vendor portfolios live here.

nodes.label: AMPM Developer Technical Specification v1.0 (SPEC)
nodes.rationale: Source of truth being extended. §3 module inventory, §4 suggested relational data model (35 rows) with a security note that client-facing and internal amounts must never share one column, §5 project creation minimums, §6 eleven roles, §7 statuses, §8 automation, §9 reports and exports, §10 configurability, §11 phases, §12 version locking and sharing rules, §15 project as parent.

nodes.label: Document access follows the owning record
nodes.norm_label: document access follows the owning record
nodes.rationale: Reading a document requires permission on owner_type/owner_id; visibility further narrows it. Download URLs are short-lived signed links (document_access_links), never permanent paths (SPEC §10, §12).

nodes.label: Approvals lock exact versions
nodes.rationale: An approval references record_type, record_id and version_number. Creating a new version of the record marks the earlier approval superseded and requires a new one. Revisions never overwrite an approved version (SPEC §12).

nodes.label: Identity documents in a restricted bucket
nodes.norm_label: identity documents in a restricted bucket
nodes.rationale: A-8: identity documents live in a separate restricted bucket with its own key, are never included in exports, and every read writes an audit_events row with action = restricted_read. A retention job deletes the file and nulls file_document_id after retention_until, which after Q17 is set only when AMPM approves deletion.

nodes.label: Media rights gate visibility (GP-20)
nodes.rationale: Only rights_status = owned, licensed or consent_obtained may be set to client, demo or public visibility; the API rejects the rest.

nodes.label: Multiple approvers (AM-7)
nodes.rationale: required_decisions on the approval and one approval_decisions row per approver. The approval becomes approved when the count of approved decisions reaches required_decisions; a single rejected or revision_requested decision moves it to that status. Both family representatives can approve (Q5).

nodes.label: Polymorphic references limited to six tables
nodes.norm_label: polymorphic references limited to six tables
nodes.rationale: owner_type+owner_id, entity_type+entity_id and record_type+record_id are used only for documents, media, comments, approvals, audit events and notifications, each with a check constraint on the allowed types. Open question §21.4 keeps one polymorphic comments table rather than per-entity tables (cleaner indexing versus multiplied code).

nodes.label: Previous wedding media require consent (GP-20)
nodes.rationale: Previous wedding media are media_assets with owner_type = hotel, rights_status = consent_obtained and consent_source_project_id set; the permission matrix publishing rule refuses client or public visibility without it. hotel_wedding_references carry a consent_document_id from the referenced client.

nodes.label: Standard columns and soft delete
nodes.rationale: created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by, deleted_at on every table. Wedding, guest and finance records are never hard-deleted; physical deletion happens only through retention jobs (A-17), which after Q17 produce proposals awaiting AMPM approval.

nodes.label: UTC storage with per-project timezone
nodes.rationale: All timestamps are stored in UTC; wedding_projects.timezone (default Asia/Kolkata) drives display (A-16, AM-13).

nodes.label: UUID v7 primary keys and FK naming
nodes.norm_label: uuid v7 primary keys and fk naming
nodes.rationale: Every table has id UUID v7 (time-ordered). Foreign keys are named <table_singular>_id. Human-readable codes such as the wedding code AMPM-2027-014 are separate unique columns, never primary keys.

nodes.label: Versioned records immutable once shared
nodes.rationale: design_versions, menu_versions, invitation_versions, vendor_proposals and hotel_proposals are immutable once shared. A new version supersedes the old one and approvals point at the exact version (SPEC §12).

nodes.label: Visibility follows the owning record
nodes.rationale: documents.visibility and media_assets.visibility are enumerations (internal, client, guest, public, demo). Everything else follows the owning record: a file attached to a vendor proposal is client-visible only if the proposal is shared and the user is a member of that project. The API enforces this on every request and every export (SPEC §6.1, §9).

nodes.label: RESTRICTED / SENSITIVE / CLIENT field markers
nodes.rationale: RESTRICTED: internal only, server-side guarded. SENSITIVE: guest health or identity data. CLIENT: client-visible when the owning record is shared. Unmarked fields are internal by default and become client-visible only through the permission matrix rules.

nodes.label: Why AMPM App
nodes.rationale: Argues that AMPM is a private, paid, client-based wedding management platform with a public marketing website and a controlled demo-to-client funnel, not a public app with open registration; this protects the proprietary hotel database and makes the software a paid business asset rather than a free public tool.

nodes.label: Critical Rule — Hotel-Discovery Subscription Does Not Automatically Activate Full Wedding Management
nodes.norm_label: critical rule — hotel-discovery subscription does not automatically activate full wedding management
nodes.rationale: Clients may select only the services they want; hotel discovery, optional hotel consultancy and complete wedding management are distinct but connected service stages.

nodes.label: Core Business Rule — Hotel Discovery and Complete Wedding Management Are Two Separate Services
nodes.norm_label: core business rule — hotel discovery and complete wedding management are two separate services
nodes.rationale: A client can purchase hotel discovery without appointing AMPM; discovery does not unlock vendor selection or wedding management; full planning access only after mutual agreement; AMPM decides the management fee separately (never calculated or displayed in the subscription); all internal costs, margins, vendor quotations and negotiation details remain private.

nodes.label: Access-Control Rules to Implement from the Beginning
nodes.norm_label: access-control rules to implement from the beginning
nodes.rationale: No public self-registration; AMPM admins create/approve accounts; module entitlements per subscription; subscription and wedding engagement tracked separately; full project access only after commercial approval and onboarding; per-wedding isolation; demo data separate; expiry/cancellation/upgrade without deleting wedding records.

nodes.label: Hotel Database as a Private AMPM Resource (not a public directory)
nodes.norm_label: hotel database as a private ampm resource (not a public directory)
nodes.rationale: Public visitors see only selected examples or previews; prospects see sample data in the demo; authorised subscribers access the module per plan; selections connect to the wedding once a project exists.

nodes.label: AMPM as a Private, Paid, Client-Based Platform
nodes.norm_label: ampm as a private, paid, client-based platform
nodes.rationale: Seeing AMPM, trying a limited demo, purchasing a subscription and receiving full wedding-project access are four different stages; the public website exists to attract, explain, demonstrate value and convert prospects into paying customers.

nodes.label: App Subscription Is Not the Complete Wedding Planning Service
nodes.norm_label: app subscription is not the complete wedding planning service
nodes.rationale: Paying for an app subscription does not automatically mean a client has purchased AMPM's complete wedding planning and execution service; these are separate commercial offerings even if they work together.

nodes.label: Three Distinct Environments (public website, demo/trial environment, private AMPM platform)
nodes.norm_label: three distinct environments (public website, demo/trial environment, private ampm platform)
nodes.rationale: The system should have three distinct environments, not one public app with open registration.

nodes.label: Added requirement: demo after mobile OTP with up to three locations and sample hotels with indicative prices
nodes.norm_label: added requirement: demo after mobile otp with up to three locations and sample hotels with indicative prices
nodes.rationale: Serves as the trial: street view where available, one or two sample hotels per location, limited hotel information, duration to be finalised; the client may request a 15 to 20 minute Zoom call before purchasing.

nodes.label: Added requirement: staff offline scope with visible sync state, conflict detection and role-limited local data
nodes.norm_label: added requirement: staff offline scope with visible sync state, conflict detection and role-limited local data
nodes.rationale: Assigned tasks, department information, readiness checklists, cue sheets, arrival and operational lists available offline with updates where supported; the app shows offline state and pending sync, never silently loses updates, detects conflicts with controlled resolution, protects locally stored data and limits offline data to the user's role.

nodes.label: Decision Q1: native iOS and Android apps with offline wedding-day access and sync
nodes.norm_label: decision q1: native ios and android apps with offline wedding-day access and sync
nodes.rationale: Native iOS and Android apps are required; offline access to essential wedding-day information with automatic synchronisation on reconnect, conflict detection and a controlled resolution process; final technical architecture to be agreed with the development team; the web remains for the public website.

nodes.label: Decision Q23: three months read-only client access after the wedding, then archive on AMPM approval
nodes.norm_label: decision q23: three months read-only client access after the wedding, then archive on ampm approval
nodes.rationale: Records are not deleted; archiving is a change of status and permissions; later access or reopening is controlled by AMPM.

nodes.norm_label: decision q3: hotel-discovery subscription rs 50,000 one-time for one month; demo via otp instead of a trial
nodes.rationale: Price and duration configurable in settings; renewal is a new purchase; after expiry the client keeps read-only access to saved hotel names and existing enquiries, nothing is deleted and renewal restores access; the OTP-reached demo serves as the trial.

nodes.label: GP-13 Guest atomic unit: individual vs family group

nodes.rationale: guests references a missing family_groups table, guest_function_attendance is per guest yet carries party_count, and allocations and travel use a polymorphic guest/group id; rooming and identity handling need individuals while headcounts need groups including children, so the individual guest must be the atomic record and the family group a grouping.

nodes.rationale: The Aadhaar framework restricts private storage and use of Aadhaar numbers; recommended position is never to store them and, where hotels need identity for check-in, to keep only document type and a masked reference under restricted access with deletion after checkout.

nodes.label: Module B — CRM, subscriptions and commercial agreements

nodes.label: payment_milestones
nodes.rationale: Payment stages for engagements (GP-6). due_date, amount, status pending/invoiced/paid/overdue/waived, invoice_id. Online milestone payment is out of the first release (Q4).

nodes.label: plan_modules

nodes.label: plans
nodes.rationale: Packages. plan_type hotel_discovery/trial/demo/package; billing_type one_time/recurring (A-3); price_amount set by AMPM, never hard-coded (Q3: Rs 50,000 one-time one month, configurable); term_days; trial_days; is_demo; status draft/active/retired; terms_version.

nodes.label: service_agreements
nodes.rationale: Paid services beyond the subscription. project_id nullable until a project exists; hotel_enquiry_id links hotel assistance to its enquiry (GP-5); scope_text; fee_amount set by AMPM (Q4); fee_structure fixed/percentage/milestones; terms_version; status draft/sent/accepted/active/completed/cancelled; accepted_by_user_id; document_id.

nodes.label: Entitlement resolution
nodes.rationale: GP-1: an active or trial subscription gives the plan_modules of its plan; an active service_agreements row gives its service's module; an active project_members row gives wedding_workspace for that project regardless of subscription state. Expiry removes the subscription modules and nothing else. Full table in permission matrix §3.

nodes.label: Hotel assistance commercial flow (GP-5)
nodes.rationale: The client's request creates a hotel_enquiries row. If AMPM charges for it, Sales creates a service_agreements row that points back to the enquiry; work beyond availability checking waits for status = active.

nodes.label: Lead to account conversion
nodes.rationale: A lead converts into a client_accounts row and keeps its history. A demo request is a lead with requested_demo = true and a lead_activities row of type demo once access is granted.

nodes.norm_label: one payments table with direction and counterparty

nodes.norm_label: am-14 tenancy: ampm only or future licensing
nodes.rationale: WHY calls the software a paid business asset, which could mean licensing to other planners; multi-tenancy is expensive to retrofit.

nodes.label: AM-8 Demo data separation
nodes.rationale: Demo data must remain separate from real client data (WHY §4): a separate database or deployment, or a tenant flag in one database?
