nodes.norm_label: cf-2 client-portal flowchart omits hotel discovery
nodes.rationale: PORTAL-FLOW has Home, My Wedding, Approvals and More but no hotels area, search, favourites or assistance request, although hotel discovery is the Phase 1 product the subscription pays for; the Home countdown presupposes a wedding date, so the portal needs a subscriber-only state and an engaged-client state.

nodes.label: CF-3 Team flowchart hides Hotels and Guests
nodes.norm_label: cf-3 team flowchart hides hotels and guests
nodes.rationale: SPEC §2.4 lists nine team areas including Hotels and Guests; TEAM-FLOW's five tabs show neither except an undefined Database entry under More and Guest/hospitality inside Weddings, so the Hotel/Destination team and the RSVP/Guest team have no home and cross-wedding guest operations are not represented.

nodes.label: CF-4 Team flowchart shows one linear path with no subscription or consultancy branch
nodes.norm_label: cf-4 team flowchart shows one linear path with no subscription or consultancy branch
nodes.rationale: TEAM-FLOW runs qualified client, create wedding record, planning, live operations, closure in a straight line, contradicting the critical rule that many clients stop at discovery or consultancy; the Level-1 flow should branch after Clients into subscription, discovery, optional consultancy, optional engagement, project.

nodes.label: CF-8 Vocabulary that exists in only one document
nodes.norm_label: cf-8 vocabulary that exists in only one document
nodes.rationale: Questionnaire, consultation as a tracked step, feedback and archive, schedule and calendar, messages and questions, countdown, Database and trial each appear in one document and are absent from SPEC; one agreed glossary is needed before Level-2 flows.

nodes.label: CF-9 Three distinct environments vs shared backend
nodes.norm_label: cf-9 three distinct environments vs shared backend
nodes.rationale: WHY §2 asks for three distinct environments and SPEC §10 for a shared backend with separate user experiences; compatible only if environment means experience, which leaves the demo-data isolation level open (AM-8).

nodes.label: GP-15 Messaging and questions have no module
nodes.norm_label: gp-15 messaging and questions have no module
nodes.rationale: PORTAL-FLOW promises messages, questions and ask a question; SPEC has no messaging module, entity or notification, only design comments and guest tickets.

nodes.label: GP-33 Native app vs responsive web vs progressive web app
nodes.norm_label: gp-33 native app vs responsive web vs progressive web app
nodes.rationale: SPEC §10 says responsive web, both flowcharts say App with tab bars, BIZ says website and connected app, WHY says the private app; no document mentions iOS, Android, app stores or push notifications, and this decision alone can change the cost estimate by a large factor.

nodes.label: RK-7 Divergent mental models between flowcharts and specification
nodes.norm_label: rk-7 divergent mental models between flowcharts and specification
nodes.rationale: If AMPM's internal picture is the flowcharts and the developer builds the spec, review meetings will surface the gap late.

nodes.label: Brief section 7: the flowcharts and the specification disagree
nodes.norm_label: brief section 7: the flowcharts and the specification disagree
nodes.rationale: The client-portal flowchart has no hotel area although hotel discovery is the paid product and its countdown assumes a wedding date; the team-app flowchart has no place for the Hotel or RSVP teams and nothing before a wedding exists. Default: the portal gains a Hotels tab and a subscriber home page; the team app keeps five tabs on phones and the nine specification areas on desktop; questions and change requests are tracked requests rather than live chat; both flowcharts are redrawn box by box.

nodes.label: AMPM Platform Requirements Audit (23 Oct 2026)
nodes.rationale: Establishes whether BIZ, WHY, SPEC and the two flowcharts are complete, consistent and precise enough to begin the SPEC §14 pre-development deliverables (wireframes, data model, permission matrix, technology recommendation, phased estimate); verdict: sufficient to start design under stated assumptions, not to start building.

nodes.label: PORTAL-FLOW: AMPM Client Portal Visual Flowchart
nodes.norm_label: portal-flow: ampm client portal visual flowchart
nodes.rationale: Level-1 navigation for the client portal (A3 PDF, undated); four tabs Home, My Wedding, Approvals, More; client-facing access only; shows no hotel discovery.

nodes.label: TEAM-FLOW: AMPM App Visual Flowchart for team
nodes.norm_label: team-flow: ampm app visual flowchart for team
nodes.rationale: Level-1 navigation for the team app (A3 PDF, undated); five tabs Home, Clients, Weddings, Tasks, More and one straight line from qualified client to closure; footer says detailed section workflows are to be designed next.

nodes.label: WHY: Why AMPM App
nodes.rationale: Access model and customer funnel, 4 sections, 21 Oct 2026; the only document defining the demo/trial stage and the no-self-registration rule, and the rule that expiry never deletes wedding records.

nodes.label: Audit verdict: sufficient to start design under assumptions, not to build
nodes.norm_label: audit verdict: sufficient to start design under assumptions, not to build
nodes.rationale: SPEC is explicitly a starting specification and BIZ §9 and SPEC §13 leave commercial decisions open. Three problems stand out: the two flowcharts and the specification describe different products; the hotel database, the core of the subscription product, has no price field; and the commercial and access decisions that drive architecture (payment mode, one-time vs recurring, client-visible finance, native vs web, RSVP identity) are still open. Counts: 9 conflicts, 44 gaps, 15 ambiguities, 8 risks, 25 decisions for AMPM, 10 blocking design sign-off.

nodes.label: Glossary and reconciled information architecture replacing the Level-1 flowcharts
nodes.norm_label: glossary and reconciled information architecture replacing the level-1 flowcharts
nodes.rationale: Both flowcharts are usable only as navigation sketches for the full-wedding-management case; the reconciled architecture must add the subscriber-only client-portal state, the Hotels and Guests areas of the team app and the branching sales funnel, with one agreed glossary before Level-2 flows are drawn.

nodes.label: Three distinct service stages: discovery, optional consultancy, full management
nodes.norm_label: three distinct service stages: discovery, optional consultancy, full management
nodes.rationale: One stage never implies the next (the SPEC 'critical rule'); stated consistently in BIZ Step 5, WHY §1 and SPEC §1.2 and §15. Many clients stop at hotel discovery or consultancy and never get a wedding project, so the product must not be designed as a pure wedding-planning tool.

nodes.label: Principle: the system is built for AMPM alone, not for licensing to other planners
nodes.norm_label: principle: the system is built for ampm alone, not for licensing to other planners
nodes.rationale: The Why note calls it a paid business asset, which could mean either; confirmed.

nodes.label: Assumed Q20: tracked requests with a conversation, no live chat
nodes.norm_label: assumed q20: tracked requests with a conversation, no live chat
nodes.rationale: A client asks a question or raises a change as a tracked request that the team answers.

nodes.label: S3 restricted identity bucket (separate KMS key, no CDN, access audited)
nodes.norm_label: s3 restricted identity bucket (separate kms key, no cdn, access audited)

nodes.label: File handling controls
nodes.rationale: Type detection by content, size limits, antivirus scan in the worker before download, metadata stripping, private buckets, 15-minute signed URLs.

nodes.label: Authorisation test suite generated from the permission matrix
nodes.norm_label: authorisation test suite generated from the permission matrix
nodes.rationale: The CSV form of permission-matrix §5 and §6 drives tests asserting allowed and denied actions, including URL and identifier tampering; policy drift fails the build.

nodes.label: Identity document controls
nodes.rationale: Never Aadhaar; minimum fields; restricted bucket; automatic deletion after checkout plus 30 days; every read audited.

nodes.label: Policy pipeline: eight-step enforcement of the permission matrix (§6)
nodes.norm_label: policy pipeline: eight-step enforcement of the permission matrix (§6)
nodes.rationale: Authenticate, principal, entitlements, guard, repository scoping, service rule check, serialiser by class set, audit; every request, file download and export runs the same pipeline.

nodes.label: Security and privacy controls by layer (§11)
nodes.norm_label: security and privacy controls by layer (§11)

nodes.label: Serialisers per visibility class (BudgetLineClientView, InternalView, FinanceView)
nodes.norm_label: serialisers per visibility class (budgetlineclientview, internalview, financeview)
nodes.rationale: Fields outside the chosen model do not exist in the response, so hiding in the interface cannot happen by accident.

nodes.label: Server-side sessions in Redis with secure HttpOnly SameSite cookies
nodes.norm_label: server-side sessions in redis with secure httponly samesite cookies
nodes.rationale: 12 hours idle for staff, 30 days for clients, revoked on role or membership change; guest tokens are exchanged once for a short session bound to the family group.

nodes.label: Signed document download via document_access_links (15-minute URLs)
nodes.norm_label: signed document download via document_access_links (15-minute urls)
nodes.rationale: The API checks the owning record, mints a document_access_links row and returns a signed URL; identity-document reads also write an audit event and alert; otherwise 404.

nodes.label: AWS Secrets Manager and three customer-managed KMS keys
nodes.norm_label: aws secrets manager and three customer-managed kms keys
nodes.rationale: Keys for database, general storage and the restricted bucket give a separate blast radius for identity documents.

nodes.label: Testing: Vitest, Playwright, adapter contract tests, generated authorisation suite
nodes.norm_label: testing: vitest, playwright, adapter contract tests, generated authorisation suite
nodes.rationale: The SPEC §12 tampering scenarios become automated tests.

nodes.label: TypeScript on Node 20 LTS end to end
nodes.norm_label: typescript on node 20 lts end to end
nodes.rationale: One language across web and API; static types make the per-class serialisers checkable at compile time; large talent pool in India.

nodes.label: Field visibility classes (§4)
nodes.rationale: Every column belongs to exactly one class; the class decides which serialiser includes it and which permission key unlocks it.

nodes.label: Seven-layer authorisation model
nodes.rationale: Principal type, global role, project scope, entitlement, record visibility, field visibility class, action; a request must pass every applicable layer in order.

nodes.label: Flow 11 — Sign-in, activation, recovery and guest access
nodes.norm_label: flow 11 — sign-in, activation, recovery and guest access

nodes.label: Denial equals absence: 404 for unseen records
nodes.norm_label: denial equals absence: 404 for unseen records

nodes.label: Integration rules
nodes.rationale: Credentials in Secrets Manager only; every webhook verifies the signature, records the raw event and runs an idempotent job; sandbox mode for development and staging; a contract test per adapter in CI.

nodes.label: Principle: authorisation lives in the API and storage layer
nodes.norm_label: principle: authorisation lives in the api and storage layer
nodes.rationale: Never only in the interface (SPEC §6.1); files reachable only through short-lived signed links; exports run through the same filters.

nodes.label: T-6 Authentication inside the API
nodes.rationale: Argon2id passwords, authenticator codes for staff, server-side sessions in secure cookies, guest access by tokenised link, no self-registration anywhere. Changed: OTP sign-in for clients and prospects; staff method to be finalised.

nodes.label: Denial is silent about existence
nodes.rationale: A client asking for a record they cannot see gets the same response as for a record that does not exist (SPEC §12 tampering test).

nodes.label: Files follow records via short-lived signed URLs
nodes.norm_label: files follow records via short-lived signed urls
nodes.rationale: Download links are minted only after the record check passes (document_access_links).

nodes.label: Separate response models per principal and permission
nodes.norm_label: separate response models per principal and permission
nodes.rationale: One endpoint, several serialisers; never one model with fields blanked out in the client.

nodes.label: Governing rule: backend APIs and file storage enforce access (SPEC §6.1)
nodes.norm_label: governing rule: backend apis and file storage enforce access (spec §6.1)
nodes.rationale: Hiding frontend controls is not sufficient; every matrix cell is a server-side check applied to API requests, file links, exports and notifications alike.

nodes.label: booking_milestones
nodes.rationale: Hold, contract, advance, confirmation. milestone_type hold_placed/contract_sent/contract_signed/advance_paid/rooming_list_due/balance_due/confirmed; due_at/completed_at; status pending/done/overdue/cancelled; amount; contract_id; document_id. An enquiry reaches confirmed only when the confirmed milestone is completed and a contract exists.

nodes.label: budget_lines
nodes.rationale: Estimate, approved, actual and internal cost per line. function_id nullable; category_id; title and description CLIENT; estimate_amount, approved_amount (locked by approval) and actual_amount (billed to the client) CLIENT; internal_cost_estimate and internal_cost_actual RESTRICTED (A-4); status draft/proposed/approved/committed/invoiced/paid/closed; vendor_assignment_id, hotel_enquiry_id, approval_id nullable; client_visible; internal_notes RESTRICTED. Open question §21.1: whether actual_amount stays client-visible.

nodes.label: contracts
nodes.rationale: Client, vendor and hotel contracts. project_id nullable for account-level client contracts; party_type client/vendor/hotel with party_id; vendor_assignment_id and hotel_enquiry_id nullable; amount; start/end_date; status draft/sent/signed/active/completed/terminated; signed_at; document_id; client_visible true for client contracts, false for vendor and hotel contracts (A-4); internal_notes RESTRICTED.

nodes.label: cost_entries
nodes.rationale: Internal actual costs, RESTRICTED table. budget_line_id; vendor_assignment_id nullable; description; amount; incurred_at; invoice_id (vendor invoice) and payment_id (outbound payment) nullable.

nodes.label: hotel_enquiries
nodes.rationale: Assistance requests and consultancy; the ten-status flow draft/submitted/awaiting_hotel/response_received/negotiating/visit_scheduled/proposal_received/client_decision/confirmed/closed. project_id nullable before a project exists; requested_by_user_id; assigned_user_id; service_agreement_id nullable (GP-5); date_from/to; dates_flexible; guest_estimate; rooms_required; functions_summary CLIENT; notes_client CLIENT; notes_internal RESTRICTED; outcome booked/declined/no_availability/withdrawn. Date-specific availability is answered inside an enquiry (GP-9).

nodes.label: hotel_enquiry_events
nodes.rationale: Enquiry timeline. event_type submitted/sent_to_hotel/hotel_response/negotiation_note/client_update/status_change/visit/proposal; occurred_at; user_id; summary; internal_only true hides the event from the client entirely; document_id.

nodes.label: hotel_proposal_lines
nodes.rationale: Proposal line items. item_type uses the same enumeration as hotel_rate_items; description; quantity; unit_amount; total_amount; client_visible.

nodes.label: hotel_proposals
nodes.rationale: Negotiated offers shown to the client, versioned. version_number; status draft/shared/revision_requested/accepted/declined/superseded; valid_until; client_total_amount CLIENT and internal_total_amount RESTRICTED (hotel net or commission basis, A-4); document_id; shared_at; decided_at/decided_by_user_id; approval_id locks the exact version; supersedes_proposal_id. Client sees proposals in shared or later status with client amounts only.

nodes.label: invoice_lines
nodes.rationale: Invoice items. description; budget_line_id nullable; hsn_sac_code (GST); quantity; unit_amount; tax_rate; line_total.

nodes.label: invoices
nodes.rationale: Issued and received invoices, split by direction not by dual amounts. direction issued_to_client/received_from_vendor/received_from_hotel (GP-17); counterparty; invoice_number UK; issue/due_date; subtotal, tax_rate (GST, A-16), tax_amount, total; supplier_gstin, recipient_gstin, place_of_supply (GP-18, dormant after Q16); status draft/issued/partially_paid/paid/overdue/cancelled/credited; payment_milestone_id nullable; document_id; client_visible only when direction is issued_to_client.

nodes.label: Module D — Hotel consultancy
nodes.rationale: Covers SPEC §3 Hotel consultancy (availability enquiry, response, negotiation, site visit, proposal, booking milestone), which SPEC §4 modelled only as hotel_enquiries. Resolves GP-5 and the acceptance test 'AMPM records negotiation and site visit without exposing internal notes'.

nodes.label: Module G — Budget and finance
nodes.rationale: Covers SPEC §3 Budget/finance (budget category, line, quote, contract, invoice, payment, cost entry) and the Closure final account. Resolves GP-17 (client versus internal invoices), GP-18 (GST), GP-19 (reference tables) and implements A-4. payments is in module B, vendor_quotes in module H.

nodes.label: project_final_accounts
nodes.rationale: Closure reconciliation, one row per project created at closure and approved by Finance before the project can close. total_client_billed; total_client_paid; total_vendor_cost, total_hotel_cost and margin_amount RESTRICTED; status draft/reconciled/approved/closed; reconciled_by; approved_by; document_id.

nodes.label: site_visits
nodes.rationale: Scheduled hotel visits. scheduled_at; status proposed/confirmed/completed/cancelled; attendees_text; outcome_internal RESTRICTED; client_feedback CLIENT.

nodes.label: An enquiry is never a booking
nodes.norm_label: an enquiry is never a booking
nodes.rationale: SPEC §7: hotel_enquiries.status = confirmed is reached only when a booking_milestones row of type confirmed is completed and a contract exists. The client sees the enquiry status, notes_client, non-internal events, site visit dates, their own feedback and proposals in shared or later status with client amounts only.

nodes.label: Invoices split by direction, not dual amounts (GP-17)
nodes.norm_label: invoices split by direction, not dual amounts (gp-17)
nodes.rationale: An invoice issued to the client is a client document; invoices received from vendors and hotels are internal cost evidence. This closes the leak path noted in audit GP-17. GST fields (tax_rate, tax_amount, GSTIN, HSN/SAC) exist so the platform could issue compliant invoices, but after Q16 they are optional and unused.

nodes.label: Material change requests raise impact flags
nodes.norm_label: material change requests raise impact flags
nodes.rationale: A material client request (A-25) sets is_material and populates impact_flags_json, raising flags on budgets, contracts, tasks and run-of-show items as SPEC §8 requires; thresholds such as material_change_threshold_pct live in configurations.

nodes.label: Project is the parent of every wedding record
nodes.norm_label: project is the parent of every wedding record
nodes.rationale: SPEC §15. Creating a project requires only name, account and a tentative date range (SPEC §5). wedding_projects.status is project-level and does not replace function, task or readiness statuses (SPEC §7). Moving to closed requires the closure checklist complete and the final account approved.

nodes.label: Client-facing and internal amounts in separate columns
nodes.norm_label: client-facing and internal amounts in separate columns
nodes.rationale: amount is numeric(14,2) with a sibling currency (ISO 4217, default INR, A-16). Client-facing and internal amounts are always separate columns, never one column with a flag, per the SPEC §4 security note, because AMPM may earn a margin (A-4) and clients must never see internal cost or margin. Applied on vendor_proposals, hotel_proposals, budget_lines, room_blocks and project_final_accounts.

nodes.label: Three client-facing amounts, two internal
nodes.rationale: The client sees estimate_amount, approved_amount and actual_amount of budget lines flagged client_visible. Internal cost columns are never serialised to a client session; the API uses separate response models per audience rather than filtering one model (SPEC §4 security note). Variance (SPEC §9) is actual_amount - approved_amount for the client view and internal_cost_actual - internal_cost_estimate internally; it is a report, not a column.

nodes.norm_label: forbidden equals absent (rule for every screen)

A rail entry appears only if the user's roles grant a permission in that area; department managers on phones see only their own sections. Project-scoped roles see only assigned weddings.

nodes.label: TW-01 Team dashboard
nodes.rationale: Cards appear only when the role has the underlying permission; role-specific alerts (new leads, expiring subscriptions, stale hotels, enquiry queue, unpaid milestones, failed notifications, incidents, readiness blocked). Finance uses dashboard cards rather than a separate workspace.

nodes.label: TW-02 Calendar
nodes.rationale: Functions, site visits, task due dates, milestones and staff shifts in one calendar with a signed ICS feed (GP-28).

nodes.label: TW-11 Lead detail

nodes.norm_label: tw-97 public content (dropped by ampm, q12)

nodes.label: Status chips with text labels
nodes.rationale: Use the status lists in permission-matrix section 7 and configurable labels in configurations; every chip has a text label, never colour alone (accessibility).

nodes.norm_label: w-12 flowchart vocabulary mapped to screens

nodes.norm_label: w-2 team workspace rail of nine areas on desktop, five bottom tabs on mobile

nodes.label: cms_pages
nodes.rationale: Public website pages, not built (Q12). slug UK home/how_it_works/services/about/contact; status draft/published; sections_json; seo_title/description; published_at.

nodes.label: cms_showcase_items
nodes.rationale: Public website showcase, not built (Q12). media_asset_id; destination_id and hotel_id nullable; source_project_id nullable for consent (GP-20); is_published; sort_order.

nodes.label: destinations
nodes.rationale: Destination catalogue. slug UK, region, state, country, description, status draft/active/inactive, public_visible (shown on the public website), hero_media_id.

nodes.label: hotel_rate_cards
nodes.rationale: Indicative commercials per hotel and season, e.g. 'Wedding season 2027'. valid_from/valid_to; currency; status draft/verified/stale/retired; verification_id; source RESTRICTED (e.g. hotel sales email); internal_notes RESTRICTED. Marked stale by a scheduled job when its verification is older than configurations.hotel_verification_max_age_days.

nodes.label: hotel_rate_items
nodes.rationale: Rate card line items. item_type enum room_rate/venue_rental/per_plate_veg/per_plate_non_veg/wedding_package/beverage_package/service_charge/tax/other (A-9, Q9); room_category_id and venue_id nullable; amount is the lower bound of a range or the single indicative value; amount_max upper bound nullable (Q9); is_indicative true for ranges shown to clients (confirmed quotations live in hotel_proposals); unit per_night/per_plate/per_event/percent; min_quantity; inclusions_text; client_visible CLIENT when true and the card is verified.

nodes.label: hotel_room_categories
nodes.rationale: Room inventory by category. room_count is the inventory in the category, max_occupancy is per room (A-27, AM-5); size_sqm; facilities_json.

nodes.label: hotel_venues
nodes.rationale: Event spaces. venue_type ballroom/lawn/poolside/rooftop/courtyard/beach/other; is_indoor; area_sqm; capacity_banquet/theatre/reception; facilities_json.

nodes.label: hotel_verifications
nodes.rationale: Freshness of each hotel field group; the source of truth for freshness. field_group profile/rooms/venues/rates/availability/media/contacts; verified_at/verified_by; source phone/email/site_visit/website/contract; status verified/unverified/stale; next_due_at = verified_at plus configurable age. 'availability' records when AMPM last confirmed general availability for a season (GP-9).

nodes.label: hotels
nodes.rationale: Hotel profile. destination_id; slug; brand; star_category; address; latitude/longitude; description_client CLIENT; status draft/active/inactive; demo_visible (A-28); public_showcase (approved for the public website); internal_rating and internal_notes RESTRICTED; total_rooms; street_view_ref (Q9); last_verified_at denormalised from hotel_verifications. About 200 hotels at the start, updated about three times a year (A-9, A-15).

nodes.label: Module C — Hotel intelligence
nodes.rationale: Covers SPEC §3 Hotel intelligence; resolves GP-8 (prices), GP-9 (availability), GP-10 (saved hotels), GP-20 (media rights), AM-5 (room capacity). media_assets is defined in module N.

nodes.label: Module P — Public website content (dormant)
nodes.rationale: AMPM decided on 25 October 2026 (Q12) that staff will not edit website content through the app. cms_pages and cms_showcase_items are kept in the model so the decision is reversible but are not built; the public website is maintained outside the platform.

nodes.label: AMPM Business Rules (BIZ)
nodes.rationale: Rule 8: do not invent business policies, so every assumption is a placeholder for AMPM's answer, not a recommendation on price or policy. §2.A: the private hotel database is never queried by public pages. §2.C: vendor negotiations must not be visible to clients.

nodes.label: Availability answered per enquiry, no calendar
nodes.norm_label: availability answered per enquiry, no calendar
nodes.rationale: GP-9, A-9: availability is not stored as a calendar. hotel_verifications.field_group = availability records when AMPM last confirmed general availability for a season; date-specific availability is answered inside a hotel_enquiries row. A live calendar would add hotel_availability_days.

nodes.label: Demo isolation at the repository layer
nodes.norm_label: demo isolation at the repository layer
nodes.rationale: Queries for a demo user are scoped to is_demo = true accounts and projects and demo_visible = true hotels at the repository layer, not in the interface (A-28). Open question §21.5: demo could use invented sample hotels seeded as inactive hotels with demo_visible = true.

nodes.label: Hotel data freshness rule
nodes.rationale: hotel_verifications is the source of truth; hotels.last_verified_at and hotel_rate_cards.status = stale are maintained by a scheduled job using configurations.hotel_verification_max_age_days (SPEC §8). A rate card whose verification is older than the configured age is shown with a stale label and its items are never presented as confirmed (SPEC §12).

nodes.label: Public website reads only public content
nodes.norm_label: public website reads only public content
nodes.rationale: The public website reads only cms_pages, published cms_showcase_items, destinations with public_visible = true and hotels with public_showcase = true, and only their PUBLIC fields. The private hotel database is never queried by public pages (BIZ §2.A). The enquiry form writes to leads; the demo request sets requested_demo = true.

nodes.label: family_groups
nodes.rationale: Invited households, e.g. 'Mehta family, Mumbai'. side partner_a/partner_b/both/other; tier configurable (VIP, family, friends); primary_guest_id; invited_by_contact_id (the account contact who added them, GP-25); max_additional_guests default 0 (A-7); source client_list/ampm_entry/import; internal_notes RESTRICTED.

nodes.label: guest_function_attendance
nodes.rationale: Attendance per guest per function, unique on (guest_id, function_id); headcounts are counted from these rows. is_invited; status no_response/attending/not_attending/tentative; responded_at; response_source self_service/ampm_call/client/import; updated_by. Indexed by project and function (§21.7).

nodes.label: guest_support_requests
nodes.rationale: Guest tickets. request_type travel/room/dietary/accessibility/correction/general/complaint (correction added by Q7); description; status open/assigned/in_progress/resolved/closed; assigned_user_id; resolved_at; resolution_text. Allergies reach caterers only through dietary requests handled by hospitality.

nodes.label: guests
nodes.rationale: One row per person; the atomic record (GP-13). family_group_id; salutation; first_name and last_name CLIENT; relation_to_couple; age_band adult/child/infant; email, phone, whatsapp_number; city, country; is_group_primary; dietary_preference veg/non_veg/jain/vegan/eggetarian/other (GP-24); allergies_text and accessibility_needs SENSITIVE; special_requests; status draft/invited/confirmed/removed; source client_list/ampm_entry/self_added/import; identification_status not_needed/pending/matched/review for self-identification on side or wedding links (Q7); internal_notes RESTRICTED.

nodes.label: invitation_recipients
nodes.rationale: Distribution status per household. invitation_version_id; family_group_id; guest_id nullable (the addressee within the group); channel; status pending/sent/delivered/opened/failed/bounced; provider_ref; rsvp_token_id.

nodes.label: invitation_versions
nodes.rationale: Versioned invitation content. content_media_id; message_text CLIENT; status draft/shared/approved/superseded; approval_id.

nodes.label: invitations
nodes.rationale: Save-the-dates and invitations (AM-12). invitation_type save_the_date/invitation/reminder/update; title CLIENT; design_item_id nullable; channels_json email/whatsapp/sms/print; status draft/approved/scheduled/sending/sent/closed; scheduled_at; sent_at.

nodes.label: menu_headcounts
nodes.rationale: Dietary headcounts for caterers (GP-24). dietary_category; expected_count from attendance and dietary preference (A-7) keeps moving; guaranteed_count is the commercial commitment given to the caterer; calculated_at. A snapshot recalculated when attendance changes and frozen when the guaranteed number is sent.

nodes.label: Module J — Invitations, guests and RSVP
nodes.norm_label: module j — invitations, guests and rsvp
nodes.rationale: Covers SPEC §3 Invitations/RSVP (invitation, recipient, guest, family group, response, attendance) and the guest request record of Rooms/logistics/hospitality. Resolves GP-13 (guest is the atomic unit), GP-16, GP-24 (dietary data), AM-1 (tokens per family group) and implements A-7. Identity documents are in module N.

nodes.label: rsvp_responses
nodes.rationale: Submission log. family_group_id; guest_id nullable; channel web/phone/whatsapp/email/in_person; token_id set for self-service; captured_by_user_id set for AMPM-assisted; submitted_at; payload_json immutable snapshot of what was submitted; locked true after submission, corrections go through the RSVP team (Q7); ip_address.

nodes.label: rsvp_tokens
nodes.rationale: Tokenised RSVP links. link_scope household/side/wedding (Q7: per side or one combined link); side bride/groom/both; family_group_id nullable for side or wedding links; token_hash UK RESTRICTED; expires_at; status active/revoked/expired; last_accessed_at; access_count; revoked_at/revoked_by. Guests never have accounts (A-13).

nodes.label: Attendance changes drive downstream flags
nodes.rationale: Attendance changes recalculate function totals and raise flags on menus, room allocations and transfers (SPEC §8) through the automation listed in permission matrix §8. menu_headcounts is a snapshot recalculated when attendance changes and frozen when the guaranteed number is sent to the caterer.

nodes.label: Dietary and sensitive guest data handling (GP-24)
nodes.norm_label: dietary and sensitive guest data handling (gp-24)
nodes.rationale: dietary_preference feeds menu_headcounts. allergies_text and accessibility_needs are SENSITIVE: visible to RSVP, hospitality and project-management staff on that project and to the client owner, never in exports by default (SPEC §9). Allergies are never listed per guest to a caterer; hospitality handles them through guest_support_requests of type dietary.

nodes.label: The guest is the atomic record (GP-13)
nodes.norm_label: the guest is the atomic record (gp-13)
nodes.rationale: Headcounts are counted from guest_function_attendance rows, so children and accompanying members are real guests rows, not a party_count. A self-service submission and an AMPM-assisted phone response both write guest_function_attendance and append an rsvp_responses snapshot, achieving 'the same guest database without duplicates' (SPEC §12).

nodes.label: Tokenised RSVP links
nodes.rationale: Originally one token per family group (A-7, AM-1): the RSVP portal shows the group's members and the functions each is invited to. After Q7 rsvp_tokens.link_scope allows household, side or wedding links; guests on side or wedding links identify themselves against the loaded list (guests.identification_status) and responses are locked after submission. Accompanying members: a group may add up to max_additional_guests rows with source = self_added; unknown guests cannot create themselves otherwise.

nodes.label: AMPM Developer Technical Specification v1.0 (20 October 2026)
nodes.norm_label: ampm developer technical specification v1.0 (20 october 2026)
nodes.rationale: Treated as the authoritative requirements document and extended rather than replaced: every table name in its data model is kept. Its roles, statuses and phases are treated as proposals because it carries no sign-off and the brief says roles and release scope must not be assumed.

nodes.label: Demo / trial mode
nodes.rationale: The Why note requires a distinct demo environment that the specification mentions only as one screen and one test and assigns to no phase (CF-1, GP-2). Placed in Phase 1 as a mode of one platform: Sales grants it from the lead record, it is time-boxed, shows a curated set of hotels with prices hidden plus one sample wedding, and every query for a demo user is limited to flagged records (U-1, A-10, A-28). A separately hosted demo is possible at extra cost.

nodes.label: Eleven proposed user roles (P-1)
nodes.rationale: CF-7: the specification lists Super Admin, Sales, Hotel team, Project Manager, Creative, Vendor Coordinator, RSVP team, Hospitality, Finance, Client decision-maker and Guest as if final while the brief says roles must not be assumed; treated as AMPM's proposal to confirm (Q6).

nodes.norm_label: demo or trial stage: granted by sales, time-boxed, sample data, expires

nodes.label: Assumptions register (§0)
nodes.rationale: Thirty assumptions A-1..A-30, each stating the default adopted, the audit question it depends on, AMPM's 25 October 2026 position (confirmed / changed / partly decided / still open / not addressed) and what changes in the model if AMPM decides otherwise.

nodes.label: client_requests
nodes.rationale: Questions, change requests and support. request_type question/change_request/support (A-20, A-21); requested_by_user_id; optional entity_type/entity_id the request is about; status submitted/under_review/clarification_requested/answered/accepted/rejected/implemented/closed/withdrawn (closed added by Q21); is_material (A-25); budget_impact_amount; impact_flags_json budget/contract/task/run_of_show (SPEC §8); assigned_user_id; responded_by/at; response_text CLIENT. Replaces both the messaging feature of the client-portal flowchart and the change-request record.

nodes.label: comments
nodes.rationale: One polymorphic threads table. entity_type enum design_version/vendor_proposal/menu_version/client_request/task/incident/hotel_enquiry; author_user_id; body; is_internal true is never client-visible; parent_comment_id; annotation_json holds an x/y pin on a design image. Also carries incident updates (module M) and internal staff notes on chat conversations.

nodes.label: configurations
nodes.rationale: Thresholds, labels and escalation rules. config_key UK e.g. hotel_verification_max_age_days, material_change_threshold_pct; value_json; scope global/project with scope_id.

nodes.label: conversations
nodes.rationale: Live chat threads (Q20). account_id; project_id nullable (subscriber conversations have no project); subject; status open/waiting_on_client/closed; assigned_user_id nullable; last_message_at; closed_at. Never carries an approval.

nodes.label: messages
nodes.rationale: Chat messages, CLIENT class on both sides. sender_type client/staff/system; sender_id; body; attachment_document_id nullable; client_request_id set when a message is turned into a tracked request; read_at.

nodes.label: Module Q — Live chat
nodes.rationale: Added for AMPM's decision that live chat is required alongside tracked requests (Q20). A conversation is a lightweight thread for immediate help; anything needing an approval history becomes a client_requests row, which a message can link to. Delivery is real time (architecture §0a); unanswered conversations surface on the team dashboard.

nodes.label: Chat versus tracked requests
nodes.rationale: A conversation never carries an approval. 'Turn into a request' creates a client_requests row with the message as its description and links back through messages.client_request_id, so the formal history stays on the request. Staff see conversations for the accounts and projects they may reach; the two family representatives see their own account's conversations. Messages are CLIENT class on both sides; internal staff notes stay in comments with is_internal.

nodes.label: Statuses fixed in code, labels configurable
nodes.norm_label: statuses fixed in code, labels configurable
nodes.rationale: Statuses are fixed enumerations in code because automation depends on them (SPEC §8); display labels are configurable through configurations. Full status lists and transitions live in the permission matrix §7.

nodes.label: Screen prefixes PUB, AUTH, DM, CP, TW, GR
nodes.norm_label: screen prefixes pub, auth, dm, cp, tw, gr
nodes.rationale: Screens are numbered by surface (public site, sign-in, demo, client portal, team workspace, guest RSVP portal), matching the four experiences that share the system.

nodes.label: Demo reached by mobile OTP
nodes.rationale: Replaces a separate trial: a prospect signs in with a mobile number and an OTP and sees a limited set of locations and sample hotels with indicative prices. Duration and the exact hotel and location limits are still open.

nodes.label: Four experiences in one system
nodes.rationale: The public website, the client portal, the team workspace and the guest RSVP pages share one system, which is why permissions and visibility are designed once rather than per surface.

nodes.label: Guest identity documents, never Aadhaar
nodes.rationale: Collected only where a hotel requires them for a wedding, passport, voter ID or driving licence only because Indian rules restrict storing Aadhaar numbers, held in restricted storage visible to named staff; the assumed thirty-day deletion after checkout gave way to AMPM-approved retention policy, which is still open.

nodes.label: Margin model with separate internal cost
nodes.norm_label: margin model with separate internal cost
nodes.rationale: Chosen over the transparent-fee model because designing for the stricter case keeps either commercial choice open: the client sees one price while cost, margin, vendor rates, quotations, commissions and negotiations stay server-side and restricted to authorised personnel.

nodes.label: Offline wedding-day operations
nodes.rationale: Required because staff work in venues with poor signal: essential wedding-day information reads offline and syncs automatically on reconnect, with conflict detection and a controlled resolution process.

nodes.label: Private RSVP link per household
nodes.rationale: Preferred to one wedding-wide link because the single link forces a guest to find their own name and needs a review queue for mistakes, while a per-household link means no duplicates and no family sees another. AMPM's answer moved this to per-side or one combined link, with the final structure still to decide.

nodes.label: Q1 - Website or native app, and is offline use required
nodes.norm_label: q1 - website or native app, and is offline use required
nodes.rationale: The flowcharts said app and the specification said responsive. A website reaches every phone on publication while native apps roughly double the front-end work. DECIDED: native iOS and Android apps are required, with offline access to essential wedding-day information, automatic sync on reconnect, conflict detection and a controlled resolution process; the final architecture is to be agreed with the development team. Still open: whether the client portal is also needed on the web.

nodes.label: Q10 - What is in the first release
nodes.norm_label: q10 - what is in the first release
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: the first release includes the demo, the subscription hotel-discovery workflow, wedding management after appointment, vendor selection, the client portal, department-based team access, RSVP, tracked requests, live chat and offline wedding-day operations; it excludes website editing, online milestone payments and GST invoicing; only Eva's authorised personnel may approve operational exceptions and that authority must be configurable. Still open: whether this scope launches as one release or hotel discovery launches first with the wedding modules following.

nodes.label: Q11 - Channels for clients and guests
nodes.norm_label: q11 - channels for clients and guests
nodes.rationale: WhatsApp and SMS registrations take two to six weeks and should start early. DECIDED: email and WhatsApp are required, SMS is proposed, and live chat is required on the home page; providers to be confirmed. Still open: the WhatsApp and SMS providers.

nodes.label: Q12 - Will AMPM staff edit the public website
nodes.norm_label: q12 - will ampm staff edit the public website
nodes.rationale: DECIDED no: staff will not edit public website content through the app in the initial scope and the website editor is not approved, which removes the assumed editor, analytics and form bot check from the first release.

nodes.label: Q13 - How people sign in
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: prospects, demo users and clients sign in with a mobile number and an OTP, replacing the assumed email and password; there is no unrestricted self-registration because AMPM creates the account or sends an invitation; staff hold individual authorised accounts with role- and department-based access. Still open: the staff authentication method, with an authenticator app recommended.

nodes.label: Q14 - Hosting, backups and recovery targets
nodes.norm_label: q14 - hosting, backups and recovery targets
nodes.rationale: Assumed an Indian region with a second Indian copy, at most fifteen minutes of data lost and four hours to recover, with accounts in AMPM's name. DECIDED: hosting, backup frequency and recovery timelines are yet to be confirmed with the developer. Still open: hosting provider and region, backup location, recovery targets.

nodes.label: Q15 - How big the system will get
nodes.norm_label: q15 - how big the system will get
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: about 200 hotels at the start and roughly 20 concurrent weddings as the planning assumption, well below the assumed five hundred hotels and forty weddings, with multiple weddings and departmental staff access. Still open: staff count and largest guest count.

nodes.label: Q16 - Currency, language and invoicing
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: Indian rupees, English as the primary language, and the platform will not issue GST invoices, which drops the assumed GST invoicing and the second-language readiness on guest pages.

nodes.label: Q17 - Privacy wording and data retention
nodes.norm_label: q17 - privacy wording and data retention
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: AMPM decides the final privacy wording and retention policy; retention and deletion require AMPM's approval, guest and wedding information must stay access-controlled, and wedding records are not deleted automatically. Still open: privacy wording and retention periods for leads, guest records and identity documents.

nodes.label: Q2 - How clients pay for the subscription
nodes.norm_label: q2 - how clients pay for the subscription
nodes.rationale: A gateway merchant account takes one to two weeks to open, so the path had to be fixed early. DECIDED: AMPM creates the account or sends an invitation link, the client enters couple names, contact, tentative dates and preferred locations and pays online by card or UPI; payment must create a record, activate the subscription once and be reviewable by authorised staff. Still open: the gateway provider.

nodes.label: Q20 - Questions and messages in the portal
nodes.norm_label: q20 - questions and messages in the portal
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: both tracked requests with conversation history and live chat are required, live chat on the home page and distinguished from tracked requests so a formal change request keeps its own approval history; more options may be added later. This overturns the assumption that tracked requests alone would do.

nodes.label: Q21 - Change requests and versioning
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: submitted, reviewed, accepted or rejected, then implemented and closed; a change to an approved item creates a new version for approval, so an approval always names an exact version.

nodes.label: Q22 - Vendors or hotels logging in
nodes.norm_label: q22 - vendors or hotels logging in
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: no vendor or hotel logins in the current version, keeping all vendor and hotel data inside AMPM's own surfaces; possible later.

nodes.label: Q23 - Client access after the wedding
nodes.norm_label: q23 - client access after the wedding
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: read-only client access for three months after the wedding rather than the assumed twelve, then the project is archived with AMPM's approval; records are not deleted because archiving is a change of status and permissions, and later access or reopening is controlled by AMPM. Still open: the exact workflow for archiving and for restoring access.

nodes.label: Q24 - Feedback and archive
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: a short feedback form after the wedding and an archived state that preserves the records, as assumed.

nodes.label: Q25 - What counts as a material change
nodes.norm_label: q25 - what counts as a material change
nodes.rationale: Assumed a budget line moving ten percent or more, or a date or venue change, with thresholds held as settings. DECIDED: thresholds must be configurable and AMPM will define the final budget-change percentages, date-change and venue-change thresholds and the approval rules. Still open: the thresholds and approval rules themselves.

nodes.label: Q3 - What the subscription is
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: hotel discovery only, Rs 50,000 one-time for one month from activation and configurable in settings; renewal is a new purchase; expiry leaves read-only access to saved hotel names and existing enquiries with nothing deleted; no separate trial because the OTP demo serves that purpose. Still open: demo duration, and whether the demo shows one or two sample hotels per location across up to three locations.

nodes.label: Q4 - How AMPM earns and what money the client sees
nodes.norm_label: q4 - how ampm earns and what money the client sees
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: hotel discovery is a separate paid service and the wedding management fee is decided by AMPM outside the app, never derived from the subscription; internal costs, margins, vendor rates, quotations, commissions and negotiations are never shown to clients; vendor profiles and service details appear only after AMPM is appointed; online collection of milestone payments is out of the first release unless separately approved. Still open: which client-facing amounts the wedding portal shows, and which hotel-assistance services beyond availability checks carry a fee.

nodes.label: Q5 - Who on the client side logs in and approves
nodes.norm_label: q5 - who on the client side logs in and approves
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: only two nominated family representatives use the client portal, one from each side, chosen by the families; no other family member holds an account without AMPM's authorisation; cost and margin are never visible to them; AMPM may record an outside-the-portal decision when a note or supporting record is attached. Still open: one shared login or two separately authenticated accounts (separate recommended for security and audit history), and whether one approval completes a decision or both must approve.

nodes.label: Q6 - Staff roles, and who sees cost and margin
nodes.norm_label: q6 - staff roles, and who sees cost and margin
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: AMPM manages the system and controls permissions; staff access is restricted by assigned responsibility and department, so a department manager on a phone sees only their own sections; the named departments are hotel, vendor, RSVP, hospitality, production, project manager and senior authorised management; internal financial information is restricted to specifically authorised personnel. Still open: the final staff role list and which users may see hotel costs and vendor costs.

nodes.label: Q7 - How guests respond and what is collected
nodes.norm_label: q7 - how guests respond and what is collected
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: invitation links are issued per side, or as one combined link when AMPM chooses; the RSVP team imports or creates the list and sends the links; guests cannot see other households or the list and cannot edit a submitted response, corrections going through a change request or the RSVP caller; the two representatives see approved summaries and cannot edit; every guest is counted individually including children, with meal preference, allergies where required, rooming and travel where applicable. Still open: the final link structure.

nodes.label: Q8 - Identity documents from guests
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: collected only where a hotel requires them for a wedding, under AMPM's control, in restricted storage, visible only to authorised staff, and never Aadhaar documents or numbers; nothing is deleted automatically and retention follows AMPM-approved policy, to be confirmed before launch. Still open: retention period and privacy wording for identity documents.

nodes.label: Q9 - Hotel data, verification and photo rights
nodes.norm_label: q9 - hotel data, verification and photo rights
nodes.rationale: The first release is only as good as this database. DECIDED: Eva maintains the existing hotel data and updates seasonal prices roughly three times a year; hotel pages show venue details, rooms, photos and videos, a food and menu grid, approximate room pricing, package price ranges, indicative venue rental, approximate per-plate pricing, capacity, facilities and map location; prices are indicative ranges with a last-verified date and never internal cost; availability is checked by the team on request or when a hotel is added to a selection; previous clients' photographs appear only with permission; spreadsheet import is supported; about 200 hotels at the start.

nodes.label: Seasonal rate card with verification date
nodes.norm_label: seasonal rate card with verification date
nodes.rationale: Room rate per category, venue rental per event, per-plate minimums for veg and non-veg, taxes and service charge, each verified on a date by a named team member and marked Stale after a configurable period, so a shown price always carries its own freshness; prices are indicative ranges and never internal cost.

nodes.label: Hotel-discovery subscription (Rs 50,000, one month)
nodes.rationale: One-time, one month from activation, configurable in settings, for hotel discovery only; renewal is a new purchase that restores access and data; after expiry the client keeps read-only access to saved hotel names and existing enquiries and nothing is deleted.

nodes.label: Tracked requests and live chat side by side
nodes.norm_label: tracked requests and live chat side by side
nodes.rationale: Both are required: live chat on the home page for immediate questions, and tracked requests with conversation history kept distinct so a formal change request keeps its own approval history rather than being lost in a chat thread.

nodes.label: Open area 4 - Who logs in on the client side and who approves
nodes.norm_label: open area 4 - who logs in on the client side and who approves
nodes.rationale: In many weddings the parents pay and the couple designs, so the default splits owner, approver and viewer with a separate switch for who may see money, one approval per decision unless AMPM says two, and on-behalf recording only with a note or document attached and visibly marked as recorded for the family.

nodes.label: Open area 7 - Flowcharts and specification disagree
nodes.norm_label: open area 7 - flowcharts and specification disagree
nodes.rationale: The client-portal flowchart has no hotel area although hotel discovery is what a subscription buys, and its Home countdown assumes every client has a date; the team flowchart has no home for the Hotel or RSVP teams and nothing before a wedding exists. Fix: a Hotels tab and a subscriber-without-a-wedding home page, the five phone tabs kept with the nine specification areas on desktop, and tracked requests with a conversation instead of the implied live chat.

nodes.label: Open area 1 - Getting in and paying
nodes.norm_label: open area 1 - getting in and paying
nodes.rationale: The documents conflict on whether the client pays from the website or AMPM creates the account first, and say nothing about demo duration or what an expired subscriber sees. Default taken: AMPM creates the account and invites, the client pays in the portal online or by transfer, hotel discovery then opens, and expiry leaves read access with nothing deleted.

nodes.label: Open area 5 - Guests, RSVP and privacy
nodes.norm_label: open area 5 - guests, rsvp and privacy
nodes.rationale: The documents never said whether a link is per wedding or per household, nor whether identity documents are needed. Default taken: load the guest list first and give each household a private link so nobody sees another family and nothing is duplicated, meal preference from everyone, allergies optional and visible only to hospitality, and identity documents only where a hotel needs them, never Aadhaar, because Indian rules restrict storing Aadhaar numbers.

nodes.label: Open area 2 - Hotels and prices
nodes.rationale: The specification's data model has nowhere to store a price or availability, and previous clients' photos need permission. Default taken: seasonal rate cards with line items and a verification date, availability answered inside each enquiry rather than kept as a calendar, a rights status on every photo and video, and spreadsheet import for hotel data.

nodes.label: Open area 3 - How AMPM earns and what the client sees
nodes.norm_label: open area 3 - how ampm earns and what the client sees
nodes.rationale: Designed for the stricter case so either commercial model works: every price carries a client-facing amount and a separate internal cost, and the internal side never leaves the server. Clients see estimates, approved amounts, invoices, payments and the next milestone; vendor quotes, contracts and received invoices are never visible.

nodes.label: Platform lifecycle in one picture
nodes.rationale: Public website, demo or trial, subscription, hotel discovery, then a branch: a client who does not hire AMPM stays a subscriber and nothing is deleted, a client who does gets a wedding project, guests, the wedding day and closure. Green boxes mark the stages AMPM's documents mentioned without defining or did not mention at all.

nodes.label: Open area 8 - Technology and operations
nodes.rationale: Whether app meant native or responsive, hosting, recovery speed, channels, sign-in, size and website editing were all unstated. Default taken: an installable responsive website in an Indian cloud region with a second Indian copy recoverable to within fifteen minutes, email plus WhatsApp and SMS, authenticator codes for staff, and sizing for fifty staff, forty concurrent weddings, fifteen hundred guests and five hundred hotels.

nodes.label: Open area 6 - The wedding day and closure
nodes.norm_label: open area 6 - the wedding day and closure
nodes.rationale: Staff work in ballrooms and lawns with poor signal and nothing in the documents mentioned working offline, so the cue sheet, readiness checks and arrival lists read without signal and sync on reconnect. A function cannot go live with a required check unmet unless a named manager records an exception, and closure is a checklist verified against the data.

nodes.label: Decisions AMPM must confirm (specification §13)
nodes.rationale: The ten listed map to Q3, Q4, Q5, Q4, Q9, Q11, Q8, Q16, Q14 and Q10; the audit found eight more that block design just as much: Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q13, Q12, Q14 and offline use (Q1).

nodes.label: GP-6: no records or rules for wedding-management payment stages
nodes.norm_label: gp-6: no records or rules for wedding-management payment stages

nodes.norm_label: q14: backup targets, hosting location and technology ownership

nodes.norm_label: q16: languages, currency, tax (gst) and international expansion timing

nodes.norm_label: q3: subscription price, duration, inclusions, recurrence, cancellation and refund terms, demo

nodes.label: Q4: financial visibility and fees - margin or visible fee, hotel service fees, management fees and payment stages
nodes.norm_label: q4: financial visibility and fees - margin or visible fee, hotel service fees, management fees and payment stages

nodes.label: FINANCE AND REPORTS area: payments, invoices, milestones, reports, final accounts
nodes.norm_label: finance and reports area: payments, invoices, milestones, reports, final accounts

nodes.label: Group 1: Getting in — the demo, payment and refunds
nodes.norm_label: group 1: getting in — the demo, payment and refunds
nodes.rationale: Groups the three commercial-entry questions (R1 demo limits, R2 gateway, R3 refunds) because they all gate the moment a prospect becomes a paying subscriber and all have lead times outside the code: demo data preparation, a merchant account in AMPM's name, and refund wording on the payment screen.

nodes.label: Group 6: Technology and operations — we propose, you approve
nodes.norm_label: group 6: technology and operations — we propose, you approve
nodes.rationale: Groups R13 to R17, the points AMPM's documents leave to be approved with the developer rather than decided alone: hosting and recovery, capacity, messaging providers, service levels, and the go-live shape. Framed as proposals to approve because the brief says AMPM will approve these arrangements with the development team before launch.

nodes.label: R1: Demo duration, locations and hotels per location (real or invented)
nodes.norm_label: r1: demo duration, locations and hotels per location (real or invented)
nodes.rationale: The demo is the first thing a prospect sees and the only trial offered. Its limits are settings, so changing them later costs nothing, but the demo data must be prepared before launch and whether the hotels are real or invented decides who prepares it: invented samples need six hotel pages written and photographed from scratch. Proposal: seven days from first OTP sign-in, extendable once by Sales; three locations (already applied); two hotels per location; real hotels flagged demo-visible with indicative price ranges and masked rate details, so the demo looks like the product and Eva's data does the work. AMBIGUITY: the brief says 'up to two sample hotels' while its closing note records that AMPM's notes mention both one hotel per city and two; duration is mentioned nowhere in AMPM's documents.

nodes.label: R13: Hosting, backups, recovery and account ownership
nodes.norm_label: r13: hosting, backups, recovery and account ownership
nodes.rationale: Hosting decides where personal data lives, how fast the platform is for users in India, what a disaster costs, and who owns the infrastructure if the development relationship ends; the specification lists technology ownership among the decisions to confirm and nothing in AMPM's documents decides it, so this is a proposal to approve. Assumed: AWS Mumbai with backup copies in Hyderabad so all personal data stays in India; database recoverable to any point in the last 35 days plus daily snapshots in the second region; files versioned and copied across regions; at most 15 minutes of data lost and the platform back within 4 hours, with a restore rehearsed quarterly; accounts, domains and provider accounts in AMPM's name with the development team as delegated administrators; the full production set-up built from Phase 1 rather than a throwaway. The same design runs on Google Cloud or Azure Indian regions — a change of names in the plan — while tighter recovery targets need a warm standby at roughly double the database cost.

nodes.label: R16: Service levels, support and wedding-day on-call
nodes.norm_label: r16: service levels, support and wedding-day on-call
nodes.rationale: New point, proposed in the architecture draft and never addressed: the brief asks for reliable backups and recovery and the specification lists maintenance and support responsibility, but no document names an availability target or says who answers the phone during a wedding. These targets drive the maintenance contract and part of the running cost. Assumed: 99.5 percent availability per month excluding announced maintenance; most requests under 0.4 seconds; portal pages usable within 3 seconds on 4G; WCAG 2.1 AA for the client and guest portals; the last two versions of the major browsers; development-team on-call on wedding days and no deployments while any wedding is live. Office-hours support lowers maintenance cost but leaves wedding-day incidents to AMPM staff until the next working day; a higher availability target changes the hosting design and its cost.

nodes.label: R3: Subscription cancellation and refund rule
nodes.norm_label: r3: subscription cancellation and refund rule
nodes.rationale: On no list until now: AMPM's business explanation section 9 lists cancellation and refund terms as still to be confirmed, rule 8 says refund terms must be confirmed before implementation, and the 25 October answers are silent. The portal has to say something at the moment of payment and Finance needs a button or a rule. Proposal: no refund once the subscription is activated, because access is immediate and the data stays with the client; full refund if AMPM cancels before activation or cannot deliver; refunds made by Finance through the gateway and recorded against the payment. A cooling-off rule adds a check at refund time; case-by-case adds a Finance permission and a recorded reason. A refund path through the gateway is designed (finding GP-7) but no refund wording is in the drafts.

nodes.label: R8: Which hotel services carry a fee beyond the subscription
nodes.norm_label: r8: which hotel services carry a fee beyond the subscription
nodes.rationale: The business explanation's section 9 lists fees for hotel research, negotiation, site visits and booking assistance among the decisions the developer must not assume, and the 25 October answers do not return to it. The answer decides whether a client can request a site visit with one tap or whether the request first produces a service agreement to accept; the amounts themselves stay outside the app, like the wedding management fee. Proposal: keep the assumption — availability checks included in the subscription, and negotiation, site visits, contract review and booking assistance behind an accepted service agreement with the fee recorded on it, even when that fee is zero for a particular client. 'All included' removes the agreement step from the hotel flow; 'everything by agreement' moves it earlier, before the first availability check.

nodes.label: Backup targets: 15-minute data loss, 4-hour recovery, second Indian region
nodes.norm_label: backup targets: 15-minute data loss, 4-hour recovery, second indian region
nodes.rationale: Q14: backups and restoration need targets for how much data may be lost and how long recovery may take; assumed fifteen minutes and four hours, with copies in a second Indian region (T-13).

nodes.label: GST fields on invoices
nodes.rationale: GP-18: no tax fields existed (Q16).

nodes.label: Rupees, English and Indian time; guest portal ready for a second language
nodes.norm_label: rupees, english and indian time; guest portal ready for a second language
nodes.rationale: Q16/A-16: 'Indian wedding destinations' is the only place the market is named.

nodes.label: Payment milestones with due dates and a refund path through the gateway
nodes.norm_label: payment milestones with due dates and a refund path through the gateway
nodes.rationale: GP-6/GP-7: payment stages for wedding management and refund handling had no records or rules; designed with the amounts and terms left to AMPM (Q3, Q4).

nodes.label: Added requirement: client completes basic wedding details before paying
nodes.norm_label: added requirement: client completes basic wedding details before paying
nodes.rationale: Couple's names, contact information, tentative dates and preferred locations are entered at account activation.

nodes.label: Decision Q2: AMPM creates or invites the account; client enters basic wedding details and pays online by card or UPI
nodes.norm_label: decision q2: ampm creates or invites the account; client enters basic wedding details and pays online by card or upi
nodes.rationale: Payments must create a record, activate the subscription once and be reviewable by authorised staff; gateway provider to be selected by AMPM; manual recording stays as a staff fallback for exceptions.

nodes.norm_label: open: payment gateway provider and transaction-handling requirements

nodes.label: CF-1 Three environments vs four experiences
nodes.norm_label: cf-1 three environments vs four experiences
nodes.rationale: WHY §2 names three environments (public website, demo/trial, private platform) while BIZ §2 and SPEC §1.1 name four parts including the guest RSVP portal; the demo appears in SPEC only as one screen and one acceptance test and in no phase, so demo deployment versus demo tenant stays an architecture and cost decision.

nodes.label: GP-2 Trial mechanics
nodes.rationale: No trial status among the SPEC §7 subscription statuses, no duration, no expiry automation, no demo dataset definition, no provisioning flow and no phase.

nodes.label: GP-4 One-time vs recurring subscription
nodes.rationale: No document says whether billing recurs; recurring billing adds renewals, failed-payment handling, proration and auto-expiry, a large scope item on its own.

nodes.label: Brief section 1: getting in and paying
nodes.norm_label: brief section 1: getting in and paying
nodes.rationale: Nobody signs up by themselves and AMPM creates every account; missing were how a demo is granted and ends, one-time vs recurring, how account creation fits online payment and what an expired subscriber sees. Default: Sales grants a time-boxed demo from the enquiry record; AMPM creates the account and invites the client, who pays in the portal online or by bank transfer; one-time fee for a fixed period; on expiry saved hotel names and read access remain and nothing is deleted.

nodes.label: Journey stage: demo or trial granted by Sales, expires
nodes.norm_label: journey stage: demo or trial granted by sales, expires
nodes.rationale: Marked new: mentioned but not defined in AMPM's documents.

nodes.norm_label: journey stage: subscription (ampm invites, client pays, hotel discovery opens)

nodes.label: Demo or trial as a mode of the private platform
nodes.norm_label: demo or trial as a mode of the private platform
nodes.rationale: Recommended instead of a separate demo deployment: AMPM-provisioned demo accounts, an isolated seeded demo dataset, time-boxed access, delivered in Phase 1, plus a trial status. A separate deployment versus a demo tenant is an architecture and cost decision, and trial expiry needs automation that no document specifies.

nodes.label: Assumed Q2: both payment paths, online gateway and bank transfer, after AMPM invites the client
nodes.norm_label: assumed q2: both payment paths, online gateway and bank transfer, after ampm invites the client
nodes.rationale: The Why note says AMPM creates every account and the specification describes a payment journey; both hold if AMPM invites first. A gateway merchant account takes one to two weeks to open; bank transfer only would remove the gateway from Phase 1.

nodes.label: Assumed Q3: one-time fixed-term subscription, Sales-granted trial, curated demo with prices hidden
nodes.norm_label: assumed q3: one-time fixed-term subscription, sales-granted trial, curated demo with prices hidden
nodes.rationale: Recurring billing needs renewals, failed-payment handling and reminders, a sizeable piece of work; the demo and trial appear only in the Why note so they had to be defined. Demo content is a data choice, not a design change.

nodes.label: Added requirement: vendor categories with contact details internal by default
nodes.norm_label: added requirement: vendor categories with contact details internal by default
nodes.rationale: Photography and videography, decor and production, catering, entertainment and artists, makeup and styling, transport and logistics and others per AMPM's service structure; AMPM may share a specific contact in an approved case.

nodes.label: Decision Q4: hotel discovery is a separate paid service; internal costs and margins never shown; no online milestone payments in the first release
nodes.norm_label: decision q4: hotel discovery is a separate paid service; internal costs and margins never shown; no online milestone payments in the first release
nodes.rationale: The wedding management fee is decided by AMPM outside the app and never derived from the subscription; internal costs, margins, vendor rates, quotations, commissions and negotiations are never shown to clients; vendor profiles are visible only after AMPM is appointed.

nodes.norm_label: gp-17 payments and invoices lack direction, parties and client/internal split
nodes.rationale: payments has no direction, payer, payee or method and contracts/invoices has a single amount; if AMPM invoices marked-up vendor services this is a margin-leak path the §4 security note is meant to prevent.

nodes.rationale: Request hotel assistance triggers paid services whose fees are undecided; the flow request, fee quote, agreement, work, status is not drawn and service_agreements has no status list or link from a hotel enquiry.

nodes.norm_label: rk-2 late financial-visibility decision forces rework
nodes.rationale: Margin model versus transparent fee changes budget_lines, invoices, payments and every client-facing finance screen; deciding after the Phase 2 model is built means rework and leak risk.

nodes.label: Brief section 3: money, how AMPM earns and what the client sees
nodes.norm_label: brief section 3: money, how ampm earns and what the client sees
nodes.rationale: Unknown whether AMPM earns a margin inside prices or a visible fee, whether clients pay milestones in the portal and which hotel services carry a fee. Default: the stricter case, every price has a client-facing amount and a separate internal cost that never leaves the server; clients see estimates, approved amounts, invoices, payments and next milestone; availability checks included in the subscription, other hotel services by agreement.

nodes.label: Server-side field-level protection of internal cost, margins, notes and identity documents
nodes.norm_label: server-side field-level protection of internal cost, margins, notes and identity documents
nodes.rationale: SPEC §4 security note and §6.1 explicitly reject hiding sensitive data only in the interface; internal commercial data must never leave the server, which is what prevents margin leaks through client-facing screens.

nodes.rationale: Designed for the strictest case so every money screen works whichever model AMPM picks: the internal side never leaves the server; a transparent fee only adds a visible fee line; removing online milestone payment turns the Pay button into bank-transfer instructions.

nodes.label: Amazon Cognito (identity, recommended)
nodes.rationale: Usable from any host; 10,000 MAU free then US$0.015/user; custom SMS sender to a DLT provider via a Lambda; effectively free for AMPM for years.

nodes.label: Firebase Auth / Identity Platform
nodes.rationale: Phone OTP goes through Google SMS ~US$0.07/message to India and cannot use the DLT provider; wrong tool for mobile-OTP sign-in in India.

nodes.label: Option A: AWS as drafted
nodes.rationale: Full enterprise posture (two Indian regions, per-bucket KMS keys, WAF, rehearsed recovery); highest ops load and bill (US$450-900/mo at launch) but no redesign.

nodes.label: Option B: AWS lite growing into A
nodes.norm_label: option b: aws lite growing into a
nodes.rationale: Recommended before the VPS was known: same Terraform at a quarter of cost during build (US$180-250/mo), Multi-AZ and the Hyderabad copy switched on at launch with no migration; Cognito identity free.

nodes.label: Option D: DigitalOcean in Bangalore
nodes.rationale: Simplest console and lowest bill with managed PostgreSQL PITR and a standby; no second region, no KMS; identity must come from Cognito or Supabase Auth.

nodes.label: Option E: Google Cloud in Mumbai
nodes.norm_label: option e: google cloud in mumbai
nodes.rationale: Equivalent posture with Delhi as a second region but a full infra redesign; Identity Platform phone OTP ~US$0.07/SMS so OTP stays in the API with MSG91.

nodes.label: Option F: Azure in Central India
nodes.norm_label: option f: azure in central india
nodes.rationale: Equivalent posture (Chennai as a second region) but a full infra redesign; right only if the developer already knows Azure.

nodes.label: Option G1: Hybrid VPS + managed data
nodes.norm_label: option g1: hybrid vps + managed data
nodes.rationale: VPS runs the application; PostgreSQL/PITR, S3 and Cognito managed elsewhere; the box rebuilt from Compose in an hour; cheapest sound build-time platform.

nodes.label: Option G2: Everything on the VPS (DECIDED)
nodes.norm_label: option g2: everything on the vps (decided)
nodes.rationale: Locked 26 Oct 2026: PostgreSQL, files (MinIO/S3) and an optional self-hosted IdP all on the box; cheapest by far and the most ways to lose data; the brief's security is met only if part 7.2 is done in full.

nodes.label: R13 hosting decision
nodes.rationale: Locked 26 Oct 2026 as G2 (dedicated VPS); the recommendation before the VPS was Option B, else C with the S3 identity hybrid; an Indian datacentre is a condition.

nodes.label: Decision D-015 (R13 locked as G2)
nodes.rationale: 26 Oct 2026: everything on AMPM's dedicated VPS with pgBackRest archives to a Mumbai bucket and rehearsed restores; sets aside architecture principle 7 deliberately.
